every_row_declares_how_it_leaves: `clears_when` names the OBSERVABLE condition that removes the row. 'the fix works' is not one; 'the mechanism is seen acting on a named trade' is. A row nobody can tell is finished never gets cleared.

items.probe_absent_reason: NO PROBE EXISTS AND ONE CANNOT BE WRITTEN THAT WOULD CLEAR THIS ROW, which is a property of the condition rather than of the effort available. The event this row waits on is a Bybit CLOSE whose qty carries an IEEE-754 artifact — MEASURED at 9 of 631 rows (1.43%) over bybit_* non-backtest trades ids 4519-5518 — and Part 1 of the same merge (round(parent_qty - consumed, 8)) STOPS most such quantities being manufactured in the first place. So the two halves interact: the more effective Part 1 is, the rarer the event that would exercise Part 2, and a probe polling for `snapped` could stay silent for a long time BECAUSE THE FIX WORKS. A silent probe here is therefore not evidence and would be worse than none — it would read as a clean negative. What CAN be graded on a cadence is the denominator: whether any close has been graded at all (any qty_state logged), which distinguishes 'the seam is being reached and finds nothing to repair' from 'the seam is never reached'. That distinction is the observation this row asks for.

soak.not_writing_is_EXPECTED_until_the_arm_is: ⚠️ DO NOT ACT ON A not_writing VERDICT BEFORE THE ARM IS CONFIRMED. The verdict only becomes a finding after BYBIT_GRADED_COVERAGE_MODE=apply and BYBIT_GRADED_COVERAGE_ACCOUNTS=bybit_1 are read back off /proc/<MainPID>/environ -- never off the .env, which says only what the NEXT restart will pick up. items.summary: scripts/ml/strategy_review_packet.py::pull_decisions filters ONLY is_backtest — it never consults account_class or is_demo — so every M7 review packet and every INDEX row blends real-money and paper PnL, against CLAUDE.md's P4 live-trade-management contract ('real and paper performance are never blended'), which /api/bot/stats, /api/bot/performance, /api/bot/trades/closed and /api/bot/strategy/attribution all honour. ⚠️ THIS CHANGES WHAT THE HEADLINE FINDING MEANS, not just a report's tidiness. The -35,446 of 'provenance-trusted losing pnl that no window could act on' — the measured motivation for widening the evidence floor's window — is essentially all paper. Population: 142 closed non-backtest trades whose order_package.created_at falls inside the 2026-09-01 packet window (2026-08-25T12:03:05Z..2026-09-01T12:03:05Z), read from a 1000-row /api/diag/journal?table=trades page spanning 2026-08-03..2026-09-02 (so the window is fully covered, not truncated), joined to order_packages on order_package_id. Split: PAPER 136 trades / -36,219.07 · REAL MONEY 6 trades / -3.11. The entire real-money population is 6 closed trades on bybit_2 across 2 legs (ict_scalp_5m x5, trend_donchian_xrp_4h x1). And 59.4% of the -35,446 is ONE leg with ONE closed trade: ict_scalp_mgc_15m at -21,070.00, verified against the journal as trade 5259 on ib_paper (MGC long 4454.8 -> 4405.8, 43 contracts, sl_cross; -49.0 points x 43 x the 10oz multiplier = -21,070.00 exactly, so the arithmetic is CORRECT — it is the account class, not the number, that is the finding).
items.detail: NOT FIXED IN THE evidence-floor-horizon PR. Splitting the gate's population changes what every packet decides on, which is the operator's call and is exactly what docs/design/evidence-floor-horizon-PROPOSAL.md §4A puts to them. ⚠️ DO NOT 'JUST ADD THE FILTER' AS A TIDY-UP: on real money the fleet closed 6 trades in 7 days, so a real-money-only gate is MORE ungradeable than the blended one, not less — ict_scalp_5m at 5 closes/7d projects to n=20 in 28 days (95% interval 13.3d-71.1d) and nothing else on real money closed at all. The right shape is two populations reported side by side with the grade taken on the real-money one, not a silent narrowing. ⚠️ AND THE PACKET'S SUMS ARE PROVENANCE-FILTERED WHILE THIS MEASUREMENT IS NOT — e.g. ict_scalp_sol_5m is 8 closes / -6,241.05 in the index and 9 closes / -6,378.79 here. Both are right for what they cover; the account-class conclusion does not turn on the difference, but do not quote the two sets of per-leg numbers as if they were one.
items.clears_when: The operator records a decision on §4A of docs/design/evidence-floor-horizon-PROPOSAL.md — either the packet reports real and paper as separate populations, or blending is explicitly DECLARED acceptable for this gate and the reason is written down. ⚠️ A MERGED FILTER DOES NOT CLEAR THIS BY ITSELF: the row is about which population the gate DECIDES on, and shipping a filter without the decision recorded would settle it by default. ⚠️ NOR DOES THE FLEET SIMPLY TRADING MORE REAL MONEY — the blend is a property of the query, not of the volume, and it would persist unnoticed at any size.

items.summary: A committed comms/strategy_reviews/<date>/ directory can hold an INDEX.json from one run beside per-strategy packets from a DIFFERENT run, with nothing stamping that a reader joining them crosses a run boundary. Measured on 2026-09-01: run #10652 (c1f95964) committed INDEX.json + all 52 packets at 12:03Z; run #10656 (7d13bc1a) then rewrote INDEX.json ALONE at 12:51Z. Population: all 52 strategies in both artifacts — 1 already disagrees, qqq_pullback_1h reading n_closed=1 / pnl=-212.52 in the index and n_closed=0 / pnl=0.0 in its own packet. The mechanism is by design (the workflow commits the index always and packets selectively), so this recurs on any day with two runs.
items.detail: MITIGATED, NOT FIXED, in the evidence-floor-horizon PR: the generator now publishes n_decisions, n_filled, execution, window_days and the evidence_horizon block ON THE INDEX, so the diagnosis no longer NEEDS the join — which removes the reason a reader would cross the boundary, without removing the boundary. scripts/ml/evidence_floor_report.py stamps sources_agree per row for anyone who still joins. The committed 2026-09-01 artifacts are deliberately NOT rewritten: a committed decision record is what that run said, and back-filling it would make a later reader believe the run published something it did not. A real fix is workflow-side — either commit the packets alongside every index rewrite, or stamp the index with the run id / generated_at that its packets came from so a mismatch is detectable rather than invisible.
items.clears_when: EITHER (a) .github/workflows/strategy-review-packets.yml is changed so a committed day directory cannot mix runs — verified by a day whose INDEX.json generated_at matches its packets' — OR (b) the index carries an explicit stamp of which run wrote the packets beside it and a reader can detect the mismatch from the artifact alone. ⚠️ A DAY THAT HAPPENS TO HAVE ONE RUN DOES NOT CLEAR THIS: single-run days are the common case and were always consistent; the defect only shows on a re-run, so 'the newest day looks fine' is not evidence.

items.summary: The evidence-horizon block (src/runtime/evidence_horizon.py; five never-collapsed classes) is published by scripts/ml/strategy_review_packet.py and read by GET /api/bot/strategy-reviews' evidence.horizon — and NO REAL RUN HAS EVER EMITTED IT. Every committed index predates the field, so evidence.horizon grades 'unknown' (we could not look) on the only record that exists, which is the route WORKING while the condition persists, not the route failing. The numbers in docs/design/evidence-floor-horizon-PROPOSAL.md come from scripts/ml/evidence_floor_report.py computing over the committed artifacts OFFLINE — the same model, not the same code path.
items.detail: Two claims, deliberately kept apart. (1) THE MODEL IS EXERCISED: 28 unit tests over the five classes and the confidence interval, plus the offline report over the real 52-leg committed run. (2) THE PUBLICATION IS NOT: no INDEX.json in comms/strategy_reviews/ carries evidence_horizon or window_days, so by_horizon_class, none_reachable_by_waiting, partly_reachable and all_reachable have never been produced by the generator on the fleet. This is the same shape as the parent row's clause (b) about floor_state, one field along. ⚠️ AND A ROUTE IS NOT A READER — nothing renders evidence.horizon yet, so the written-and-never-read defect is moved one hop, not eliminated.
items.clears_when: A committed INDEX.json carries evidence_horizon on its rows AND an evidence_horizon_summary, and a read of GET /api/bot/strategy-reviews against that date returns evidence.horizon.horizon_state with a value OTHER than 'unknown'. ⚠️ A PASSING TEST DOES NOT CLEAR THIS and neither does reading the merged diff — the harness is not the fleet. ⚠️ NOR DOES THE OFFLINE REPORT: scripts/ml/evidence_floor_report.py computes the same model from the same numbers and deliberately writes nothing into comms/, so a report that looks right says nothing about whether the GENERATOR published the block.

items.detail: ib_paper MHG held a 29-lot position against TWO disjoint OCA groups — 58 lots of resting stop, 200%. The stranded leg was cancelled 2026-08-26 in a maintenance window (issues #10332-#10338) and the position now rests under ONE group (oca-protect-t4796, STP 6.364 + LMT 7.1415) matching journal trade 4796. items.detail: ib_insync's openTrades() reads an ACCUMULATED cache and reqAllOpenOrders only ADDS to it, while cancel callbacks reach the SUBMITTING client only — so the read-only client the route uses never learns of a cancel it did not issue. Measured: the route and a fresh client differed by EXACTLY a cancelled pair while agreeing on all six other orders. The envelope now carries a stale_read_caveat. The ENFORCING path (the naked sweep, on the trader's own client) is unaffected.

items.observation: RE-AFFIRMED / NOT OBSERVABLE 2026-09-06 by session_01UaZ9boMDajiCZsjVkr4Fnz. WHAT I DID OBSERVE, and it is worth recording because it bears on every row that reads this route: two calls to /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper 53 seconds apart returned DIFFERENT read_states -- 2026-09-06T08:59:13.201342Z gave {read_state:'could_not_look', orders:null, error:null} and 2026-09-06T09:00:06.728981Z gave {read_state:'orders_read', 6 orders}. The three-state contract is therefore working as designed: the failing read declared itself as 'we did not look' rather than returning an empty book, which is exactly the collapse this repo's collapsed-states rule exists to prevent. A session that had taken the first response as 'no protective orders rest' would have concluded ib_paper was naked on three positions. The route still carries its stale_monotonic caveat in every payload.

items.summary: The generated SESSION-BRIEF block in CLAUDE.md is the mechanism this session shipped in place of a cap and an adjective, and NO fresh session has ever read it. Shipped and working are different states; only a real session acting on the block settles it.
items.observation: 2026-09-09, MI-225 audit: AN OBSERVATION IS RECORDED WITH ITS CONTAMINATION CAVEAT STATED, so a later session can judge it rather than inherit my judgement. WHAT HAPPENED: this session's spawn prompt named a work object, the full-system-audit skill and three failure classes to carry - it named NO monitoring item and did not mention the session brief. The session read CLAUDE.md at start, read the generated SESSION BRIEF block there, and has reported on ten due monitoring items in this file with fresh measurements, citing the brief as where it saw them. THE CAVEAT, and it is why I am not calling this row cleared myself: a SessionStart hook told me to read the root CLAUDE.md in full. That is not the same as being pointed at the BRIEF - the hook names the file, not the block, and nothing told me any row was due - but it is not a perfectly cold arrival either, and this row exists because that distinction gets blurred. RECORDED, NOT CLEARED. The manager or operator should decide whether a hook-instructed full read of CLAUDE.md counts as 'not pointed at this mechanism by its prompt'; if it does, this row clears on this observation.
items.clears_when: A session that was NOT pointed at this mechanism by its prompt reports on a due monitoring item, citing the CLAUDE.md brief as where it saw it. WARNING: the handoff prompt written at the end of this session names the MHG item explicitly, so the FIRST session after this one cannot be the clean test -- it has been told. The uncontaminated observation is a later session that arrived cold. Record which it was.
items.why_it_matters: If the block is not read, the register is exactly the thing it replaced: a file that looks like a follow-up mechanism and is not one. That failure is invisible -- an unread brief and a brief with nothing due are byte-identical from outside, which is the 'we did not look' vs 'we looked and found nothing' collapse this repo has a guard family for.
items.probe_absent_reason: MISSING CAPABILITY: a witness for a session's OWN REASONING PROVENANCE — which does not exist anywhere in this system and is not merely unbuilt here. clears_when asks for a session that was NOT pointed at the mechanism reporting on a due item AND CITING THE BRIEF AS WHERE IT SAW IT. Every artifact a session leaves — a commit, a PR body, an OPEN-ITEMS observation — records what it CONCLUDED, never which input it read to get there, and the criterion turns entirely on that provenance: the identical sentence is the clearing observation from an uncontaminated session and worthless from a prompted one. A probe grepping any of those surfaces for a citation would be reading a self-report as evidence of its own cause. The row also names its own contaminant (the handoff prompt that already told the next session), which no machine can check. This is PERMANENTLY unprobeable under the current artifacts, and would become probeable only if sessions recorded a structured 'read from: session-brief' provenance stamp — which would then be a self-report too, so the honest position is that a human reads it.

Arming without resolving that trades one safety defect for a worse one. probe.checks: A stray_oca_soak row exists in which the sweep GRADED a non-keyed protective group as a stray (`decision: stray_unkeyed`) AND actually cancelled it (`acted: true`) rather than being held back by PROTECTION_STRAY_GROUP_ACCOUNTS. Those are two different facts and both are required: `acted` is the EFFECT, `decision` is the finding, and a row carrying the finding at `mode: annotate` is the STAGED state, not a cancel. The positive control (`decision` present with any of its three values) is what separates 'the sweep ran and found no strays' from 'the log is absent or unreadable' — without it an empty log emits a confident negative, which is the state this row has been in since 2026-08-26.
probe.is_not: A PASS does not clear this row. `clears_when` asks for the position's REMAINING protection to be confirmed correct afterwards — that the sibling keyed group and the keep-target still rest at the journal's levels — and this probe reads the sweep's OWN account of what it did, never the venue. The soak records `cancel_calls_made` and a `verify_state`, but `BL-20260825-PLACE-PROTECTIVE-COUNTS-THE-CANCEL-CALL-NOT-ITS-EFFECT` is exactly the defect of trusting a self-report, so the confirming read is /api/diag/ib_open_orders on a FRESH client (that route's own view is monotonically stale, BL-20260826-DIAG-IB-OPEN-ORDERS-SERVES-A-STALE-MONOTONIC-ORDER-VIEW). It also cannot see whether the cancelled group was genuinely this trade's abandoned protection rather than something a human placed — `ungrouped` is refused for that reason and `stray_unkeyed` is an inference from the group NAME.

items.probe_absent_reason: A PROBE IS WRITEABLE AND DOES NOT EXIST, and that absence is itself the finding this row now carries — so it is declared rather than left blank. The check is mechanical and I performed it BY HAND this session: net every non-backtest status='open' row in `trades` per (account_id, symbol) and compare to /api/diag/exchange_positions; 26 of 27 pairs agreed and one did not. Nothing in the repo runs that comparison on a cadence, which is exactly why a 43-lot divergence stood ~26h with reconcile_status NULL on both rows. ⚠️ THE PROBE MUST NOT BE THE OVER-COVER PAGE, which is what currently reports this position: that page keys on DISJOINT OCA GROUPS, so it would fall silent the moment one group is cancelled while the journal is still wrong — a green reading from it would mean 'the protection was tidied', never 'the journal agrees with the venue'. ⚠️ AND IT MUST DECLARE AN UNREADABLE ACCOUNT AS UNREADABLE rather than as agreement: ib_live, oanda_practice and breakout_1 return no positions, and folding 'we could not look' into 'no divergence' is the vacuous-negative class CLAUDE.md § 'Green is not evidence' names. Writing that probe is the natural companion to the structural fix in BL-20260908-IB-PAPER-MGC-JOURNAL-HOLDS-43-LOTS-THE-BROKER-DOES-NOT-AND-A-43-LOT-STOP-RESTS-AGAINST-THE-PHANTOM, and is deliberately proposed there rather than improvised here.
items.observation: 2026-09-08 (MI-192b /system-review) — THE SAME DEFECT CLASS, 43x LARGER, WITH A LIVE STOP ON THE PHANTOM. Population: all 31 non-backtest status='open' rows (/api/bot/db/table/trades) netted per (account_id, symbol) against /api/diag/exchange_positions captured 2026-09-08T10:29:57Z. 26 of 27 comparable pairs reconcile EXACTLY across bybit_1/2/portfolio, ib_paper and alpaca_paper/portfolio — the positive control, and the same control logic the 2026-08-26 reading used with MHG/MES. THE DIVERGENCE: ib_paper/MGC journal 54.0 vs venue 11.0, from two open rows — id=5353 (mgc_pullback_1d, 11.0 long, opened 2026-09-02T13:41:20Z) and id=5531 (ict_scalp_mgc_15m, 43.0 long, opened 2026-09-07T08:26:33Z). The venue position equals 5353 ALONE, so 5531's 43 lots do not exist at the broker. BOTH carry reconcile_status=NULL — nothing has flagged either, ~26h in. WHY IT IS NOW LOUD: PROTECTION_REASSERT re-armed a 43-lot bracket against 5531 at 2026-09-07T11:55:19Z (protection_reassert_soak: decision=reassert, acted=true, applied_state=both_legs_resting, ocaGroup oca-protect-t5531). If that stop fires it SELLS 43 MGC contracts the account does not hold, opening a naked SHORT. The IB over-cover page IS firing correctly about it — 4 rows 2026-09-07T12:00:59Z through 2026-09-08T06:09:21Z: 'position 11.0 but resting STOP qty totals 54.0 (491%) across 2 DISJOINT OCA groups oca-protect-t5353, oca-protect-t5531'. Note the 5m40s gap between the reassert and the first page but do NOT read it as causation: I did not establish which mechanism placed t5353, and the reassert re-arming a bracket for a row the journal calls open is the mechanism behaving correctly on bad input. ROOT CAUSE, VERIFIED IN CODE — and it is what this row PREDICTED in 2026-08-26: order_monitor._reconcile_netting_partial_closes selects accounts by str(a.get('exchange','')).lower() == 'bybit'. There is NO interactive_brokers equivalent, and IB futures net per contract identically, so one venue position backs N journal rows and per-order close detection cannot see that ONE row lost its backing while another still has some. This row said journal_qty_divergent 'exists only in _check_broker_naked_bybit_positions, never on the IB path' — still true, and the cost has grown from 1 lot to 43. FILED as BL-20260908-IB-PAPER-MGC-JOURNAL-HOLDS-43-LOTS-THE-BROKER-DOES-NOT-AND-A-43-LOT-STOP-RESTS-AGAINST-THE-PHANTOM. NOTHING WAS ENACTED: no leg cancelled (standing prohibition, and BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG is what happened the one time this class was auto-remediated), no journal row closed. ib_paper is PAPER, so no real money is at risk in THIS instance; the code path is account-agnostic.

items.summary: SUCCESSOR to OI-20260829-TRAINER-IS-NOW-A-DECIDED-DEPENDENCY-AND-IS-UNMONITORED, which CLEARED 2026-09-03 on its clause (a): trainer-capture-watch.yml run 33719856283 graded the trainer's order-flow capture from the DATA's mtime and PROVED it fires — planted-stale control graded `stale` at age=10800s against a 1800s threshold while the fresh control graded `fresh` at age=0s, controls_ok=true, and the receipt landed on main. ⚠️ THAT WAS A HUMAN PRESSING A BUTTON. The SCHEDULE has never produced a successful run: the one and only scheduled attempt (run 33716069132, event=schedule) fired 2026-09-03T04:43:09Z against a first eligible slot of 00:23Z — 4.34 HOURS LATE — and failed. An alarm that runs only when dispatched monitors nothing, and the capture is a forward-only stream nothing can re-derive.
items.detail: THREE FACTS, AND ONLY THE FIRST IS SETTLED. (1) THE GRADER FIRES — proven, and not by a harness: the controls are planted on the real trainer host over the real SSH hop and graded by the same function that grades the watched path, so a self-test passing in CI is not what this rests on. (2) THE CADENCE HAS NEVER WORKED. Declared cron `23 */6 * * *`; the workflow landed on main 2026-09-02T21:35:16Z, so 00:23Z was its first eligible slot and the single scheduled run came 4h20m09s later and FAILED — at the pre-fix missing-pytest step, so that failure predates PR #10875 and is NOT a defect in the fix. CLAUDE.md's own rule is that a cron is not evidence of a run, and probes.yml's first scheduled run fired ~4h50m late and ONCE instead of daily, so LATE-AND-ONCE is this repo's OBSERVED failure shape rather than a hypothetical worry. (3) THE PAGE HAS NEVER GONE OUT. Both Telegram steps — `Telegram alert — the CAPTURE is not healthy` (keyed on capture_bad) and `Telegram alert — the ALARM ITSELF is not trustworthy` (keyed on controls_broken) — read `skipped` in run 33719856283, and neither has executed on ANY run of this workflow. The controls prove the GRADER separates stale from fresh; they say nothing about whether a page reaches the operator, which is a different step on a condition that has never been true. Do NOT read `controls_ok=true` as evidence the alert works.
items.clears_when: BOTH, and they are different facts — say WHICH you cleared rather than clearing the row on the easier one. (1) A SCHEDULED run of trainer-capture-watch.yml is OBSERVED completing successfully AND its receipt docs/claude/work/TRAINER-CAPTURE-WATCH.json is on main carrying THAT run's `generated_at` — read the run history and that stamp, NEVER the cron expression, and record how late it fired against its declared slot. ⚠️ A workflow_dispatch run clears NOTHING here: dispatch is precisely what is already proven, and the failure class being watched is a cron that does not fire. (2) The capture-stale PAGE is observed EXECUTING — a `Telegram alert` step reaching a non-skipped conclusion — whether from a genuinely stale capture or from a deliberate exercise that makes capture_bad true. ⚠️ A GREEN RUN WITH BOTH ALERT STEPS `skipped` IS THE HEALTHY CASE AND CLEARS (2) NOT AT ALL; that is what every run so far has been, so 'it passed again' is not progress on this half. ⚠️ AND THE STEP REPORTING `success` IS NOT THE OPERATOR RECEIVING IT — that distinction keeps other rows in this file open; record which of the two you established. ⚠️ IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES the 6-hourly cadence is wrong, or that the watcher should not run, this row does NOT clear — it CHANGES: the capture is then unwatched on a schedule, which is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one rather than left looking like a cadence about to start.
items.why_it_cannot_be_closed_by_time: The capture is FORWARD-ONLY: an hour it does not write is an hour nothing can re-derive, so the cost of a cadence that never starts accrues silently and is unrecoverable. Waiting does not produce the scheduled run — only reading the run history establishes whether one happened.

    [control] control_stale: stale age=10800s read_state=read path=/tmp/mi81_control_stale.jsonl

RECEIPT ON MAIN, read with `git cat-file -p origin/main:docs/claude/work/TRAINER-CAPTURE-WATCH.json`: generated_at 2026-09-03T05:41:00Z, run_url naming run 33719856283, capture_state fresh, controls_ok true. It got there through commit-to-main's own PR #10892 (opened 05:41:04Z, merged 05:43:07Z, 2m03s) — so the SSH hop, the plant on the live trainer, the grader and commit-to-main were ALL exercised for the first time on this run, and all four worked. GUARD ARMED ITSELF: scripts/ci/check_trainer_capture_watch.py now grades `fresh` (newest recorded run 0.1h old, window 15h) where it graded `never_ran` before any receipt existed. THE SCHEDULED RUN, measured not assumed: run 33716069132, event=schedule, created 04:43:09Z, conclusion FAILURE; the workflow landed on main 2026-09-02T21:35:16Z (git log on the workflow path), so under cron `23 */6 * * *` its first eligible slot was 00:23Z and it fired 4h20m09s = 4.34h late. It failed at the missing-pytest step — head_sha 42b8dbfc, before PR #10875 merged at 05:40:12Z — so it is evidence about the CADENCE and says nothing about the fix. NOT OBSERVED, and this is the half the row exists for: no scheduled run has EVER succeeded, and neither Telegram alert step has EVER executed on any run (both `skipped` in 33719856283, which is the correct behaviour on a healthy capture and therefore proves nothing about the page).

probe.checks: CLAUSE (2) ONLY — that the capture-stale PAGE has actually EXECUTED. It looks for the literal the `Telegram alert — the CAPTURE is not healthy` step emits, in the job logs of trainer-capture-watch.yml. That step is gated on `steps.grade.outputs.capture_bad == 'true'`, a condition that has never been true, so the string cannot appear unless the page really fired. The positive control is `controls_ok=`, which the `Grade freshness` step prints on every run that reaches it: if THAT is missing the reader is proven blind and the verdict is `could_not_look` rather than a confident negative — which matters here, because 2 of the workflow's first 3 runs died before the grader ever ran.
probe.is_not: ⚠️ A PASS HERE DOES NOT CLEAR THIS ROW, AND A FAIL IS THE EXPECTED READING TODAY. It covers clause (2) and says NOTHING about clause (1), the cadence — which is the half the row primarily exists for. Nothing this probe can reach distinguishes a SCHEDULED run from a `workflow_dispatch` one: `probe_actions_log.py` has no `--event` filter, and the receipt docs/claude/work/TRAINER-CAPTURE-WATCH.json records capture_state, controls_ok, generated_at and run_url but NOT the triggering event. ⚠️ THE ONE-LINE CHANGE THAT WOULD MAKE CLAUSE (1) PROBEABLE is to have the workflow write `github.event_name` into that receipt; until then clause (1) is settled by READING THE RUN HISTORY BY HAND, and this row must not be cleared on a green probe. ⚠️ Nor does a pass mean the operator RECEIVED the page: the step emits the literal before `notify_session.py` reports anything, and the send is explicitly non-fatal (`|| echo ::warning::telegram notify failed`), so the string proves the step RAN, not that a message landed.

items.summary: alpaca_live go-live: the T+1 model now EXISTS (PR #10408, merged + deployed 2026-08-29, running at `annotate`). The row stays OPEN because `clears_when` requires the model be SHOWN ACTING, and at `annotate` it binds nothing by construction — so shipping it cannot clear this. Operator settled the fork: CASH, permanently.
items.detail:
FOUR DECISIONS TAKEN 2026-08-29, recorded here so no session re-asks them. The operator's complaint that prompted this — that cash had been said 'a million times' — is the cost of NOT having recorded it. (1) FUNDING MODE: CASH. Settled, not provisional. capacity.multiplier=1 was measured 2026-08-29T00:22:41Z. Consequences that follow and are NOT re-litigable: no shorting, gross-exposure multiple can never exceed 1.0x so max_gross_exposure_pct is decorative, and PDT is INERT (BL-20260823-NO-PDT-MODELLING-ON-ALPACA does not apply under this branch). (2) SIZE BOUND: a per-trade cap expressed as a PERCENT OF EQUITY, not a fixed dollar figure — chosen so it scales if the account is later funded rather than going stale, and so oversized intents are sized DOWN and still place rather than being refused by the venue. Value not yet chosen; Tier-3. (3) T+1: MODEL IT BEFORE ANY LEG GOES LIVE. The operator declined the cheaper 'restrict to 1d legs and defer' option I recommended. This is the blocker this row tracks. (4) FUNDING AMOUNT: keep $200.10 for now; revisit after real fills reconcile. At the 0.9 cash wall that is ~$180 usable, so any instrument priced above it is mechanically untradeable at one whole share — indicative prices from the retracted Phase 3 doc put GLD ~$423 and SPY ~$640 in that category, NOT re-measured. ROSTER INTENT: one cheap, affordable, non-USO, daily-cadence leg as an explicit PLUMBING TEST — to prove fills reconcile against exchange truth, that whole-share sizing behaves on a cash book, and that silent_refusal_alert grades the account healthy. It is NOT an edge bet and must not be reported as one: stripped of uso_trend_1h (excluded from real money on standing non-financial grounds), the 16-leg candidate set has NO positive measured record on either paper population. The specific leg is not yet chosen and adding it is Tier-3 in its own right — alpaca_live is mode: live with strategies: [], so that empty list is the ENTIRE gate and the first leg added IS the live-trading moment, with no mode flip in front of it. 

UPDATE 2026-08-29 (same day, later): THE MODEL SHIPPED — PR #10408, `src/runtime/cash_settlement.py`, merged and deployed (VM confirmed on the merge sha, restart_pending false). Basis is `min(venue_buying_power, venue_cash - our_unsettled)`, which is correct under all four combinations of (Alpaca nets unsettled proceeds / does not) x (we saw the sale / did not) — asserted as a 4-case parametrized test, because the distinguishing state has NEVER existed on this account (cash == buying_power == regt_buying_power == equity == 200.10, all four identical) and both paper mirrors are MARGIN accounts that cannot exhibit cash-account behaviour. Trading days come from the venue's own /v2/calendar because src/runtime/market_hours.py models no holidays and counting T+1 with it would credit proceeds a day EARLY across a holiday, manufacturing the violation. 

THE REMAINING TWO DECISIONS ARE ALSO NOW TAKEN (2026-08-29, popups): per-trade cap = 100%, i.e. NO cap beyond the cash account's own 1.0x limit; `risk_pct` STAYS 0.05. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-31: that half is STALE and was stale in the dangerous direction — do NOT re-quote it. The DEPLOYED value is **0.02**, confirmed on /api/bot/config (`risk_pct: 0.02`) and in config/accounts.yaml, which records it as operator-directed 2026-08-29 restoring the GATE-CLEARED value because 0.05 sat on unmeasured survival ground. Field beats comment. The coherence argument below still holds and is unaffected: cash, not risk, is the binding term — the reachable symbol set is IDENTICAL at 2% and 5%. Decision (2) in the block above is therefore RESOLVED and its 'value not yet chosen' is stale. Why that pair is coherent rather than reckless at this size, so nobody 'fixes' it: the sizer demands ~26.7 TLT shares (~11x the account) and the CASH BALANCE clamps it to 2, so realised risk at the declared stop is ~$0.75, not the $10 the 5% implies — confirmed by the observed qty 2.0 journal rows, not inferred. Plumbing-test leg CHOSEN: `tlt_pullback_1h` (TLT ~$83 so 2 shares fit; n=171, the best-evidenced leg on the roster). 

WHY THIS ROW STILL DOES NOT CLEAR, and what would: `clears_when` asks for a would-be order REFUSED with a logged cause. At `annotate` the gate computes and writes a soak row and changes no sizing, so it can never produce that observation. Clearing needs the Tier-2 flip to `apply` (allowlisted to alpaca_live only) AND a real case. WARNING FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: `would_have_reduced_usd` will read 0.00 on alpaca_live however long anyone waits — `recent_sales` requires status='closed' with a non-null exit price inside a 10-day window and that account has NONE (all 23 recent rows are `rejected`; its last real position closed in July). T+1 binds only AFTER a sale, so an account that has never traded cannot demonstrate it. That is circular by construction, not a gap. The mechanism evidence lives on the PAPER accounts, which do sell — 6 closed sales in 10 days, up to $111,069.37. 

A REPO TIMER NOW CARRIES THE PRECONDITION: PR #10412 adds `.github/workflows/alpaca-settlement-soak-watch.yml`, weekdays 14:30 UTC. It grades the soak against the newest alpaca dispatch FIRST, so an empty soak is never collapsed: `not_yet_exercised` (no dispatch since deploy — silent, not a failure) vs `never_wrote` (a dispatch DID happen — a finding, fails the job). This exists because the precondition was being carried by a session check-in, which dies with the session.
items.clears_when: T+1 settlement is MODELLED in code and the model is shown acting — a would-be order that the account could not settle is refused with a logged cause, observed on a real or replayed case, not merely unit-tested. A passing test is not an observation of the live mechanism. This row does NOT clear on the leg going live, and NOT on the funding decision.
items.why_it_cannot_be_closed_by_time: Nothing accrues that builds the model; it is work someone has to do, and until it exists the operator's own stated precondition for go-live is unmet. This lane has already stalled once by leaving a decided question looking open — that is exactly what this row replaces.

THREE route to bybit_2 = REAL MONEY (trend_donchian, trend_donchian_eth_4h, trend_donchian_xrp_4h). It is DEPLOYED, not PROVEN, and those are different facts. items.detail:
⚠️ THE 10TH APPROVED LEG WAS NOT SHIPPED. trend_donchian_eth_prop's sm1.5 cell is real (path_b_wf_pass, wf 5/6, +13.4198) but it is a config-only EXIT variant whose design premise is ENTRY-IDENTITY with trend_donchian_eth (atr_stop_mult is an entry param there, deliberately), it was graduated to execution: live on a prop EV/survival gate measured on that construction (relay #8975, run_ev_montecarlo under breakout.yaml, +$883 @ P(net>0)=0.8477 over 1,110 trades), and breakout_1 can be PERMANENTLY DISABLED by a drawdown breach. A stop change moves the R denominator, the size and the breach probability, so that gate would no longer describe what runs. Caught by test_unit_c_prop_exit_variants, which was RIGHT; the test was NOT weakened. Unblocks only on a fresh run_ev_montecarlo under breakout.yaml plus operator approval on that evidence.

⚠️ TWO OF THE TEN SHIPPED CHANGE STRATEGY SHAPE, NOT STOP WIDTH, and one of those is real money: ada_pullback_2h tp_r 50.0 -> 4.0 and trend_donchian_xrp_4h tp_r 50.0 -> 3.0 introduce a take-profit where the leg previously had NONE (50 is the no-target sentinel). Capping a TREND leg at 3R truncates exactly the rare large winners trend-following depends on. The walk-forward passed it (path_b_wf_pass, wf 5/6) and the operator approved the full set; this row exists so the first real close on that leg is LOOKED AT rather than assumed fine.

⚠️ avax_pullback_2h sm2 shipped at d_net_r +1.0084 against my own written recommendation to DROP it. The operator reaffirmed the full 15 after reading that. It is execution: shadow, so nothing live moves — recorded so the decision is attributable, not re-litigated.

⚠️ EVERY ONE OF THESE RESTS ON A RUN WHOSE CLEAN-LEG CONTROL FAILED as specified, with a fold-level substitute the operator accepted on 2026-08-29. That is a weaker evidentiary base than B4 had, and it is the reason to watch rather than to wait.

The matrix cells are now `shipped`, so `matrix-bracket-values` enforces the 17 shipped bracket_geometry cells against config/strategies.yaml on every PR (state the population: the matrix carries 39 shipped cells across ALL levers; this guard covers the bracket_geometry column only, and per BL-20260829-MATRIX-BRACKET-VALUES-READS-ONLY-THE-BACKTICKED-CELL-SPELLING it reads only the backticked cell spelling. An earlier version of this row said "all 18 shipped cells" — wrong on both the count and the scope, in the direction of overstating coverage) — a silent drift back is now a CI failure rather than a discovery.
items.clears_when: BOTH: (a) /api/bot/config read back shows the new atr_stop_mult/tp_r on all 10 legs, confirming ict-git-sync carried them to the running trader; and (b) at least one closed trade on a real-money leg that was **OPENED AFTER the deploy of 892c9a2c**, read against broker truth. ⚠️ (b) SAYS *OPENED*, NOT *CLOSED*, AND THAT WORD IS THE WHOLE CRITERION — it previously read 'at least one CLOSED trade exists on a real-money leg under the new geometry', which a trade opened BEFORE the deploy satisfies on its face while carrying the OLD geometry. That is not hypothetical: trend_donchian_eth_4h trade 4904 (bybit_2, ETHUSDT) CLOSED 2026-08-30T09:48:15Z — after the deploy, on a real-money e35 leg — and is disqualified TWICE OVER. It was OPENED 2026-08-21T21:54:54Z, nine days earlier, so its bracket is the pre-e35 2.5 atr_stop_mult; and per PR #10482 it was an OPERATOR FLATTEN executed to satisfy the flat-symbol guard for the Bybit hedge switch, i.e. not a strategy exit at all. Its exit_reason reads 'reconciler_filled', which describes HOW the row closed and misdescribes WHY. A session applying the old wording could have cleared this row on it. Explicitly NOT sufficient: the PR merging, CI green, or the guard passing — the guard compares the matrix to the repo, and neither of them is the running trader. Also NOT sufficient: a closed trade whose pnlProvenance is 'fabricated' or 'unverified', or one closed by an operator action rather than by the strategy — read PB-20260830-XRP-4H-FIRST-CLOSE-UNDER-NEW-BRACKET-UNVERIFIED before grading any first close, and do NOT grade the exit off exit_reason alone. ⚠️ (b) IS SHARPENED A SECOND TIME, 2026-09-01, ON OPERATOR DECISION, AND THE ADDED CLAUSE IS NOW ALSO PART OF THE CRITERION: the qualifying trade's leg must have cap_r > its own tp_r — i.e. the DECLARED tp_r must be what set the target, not the venue clamp. The effective target is min(cap_r, tp_r) with cap_r = 0.099*entry/risk (src/runtime/tp_venue_cap.py), so on a trade where cap_r < tp_r the e35 tp_r value never reaches the wire and the identical bracket would have been placed under the OLD 50R sentinel. Such a trade cannot verify the tp_r half however cleanly it closes — the same shape as the first sharpening, where a trade satisfied the letter while proving the wrong thing. NOT HYPOTHETICAL: trade 5250 satisfies every other clause of (b) and was measured at cap_r = 2.892634 against tp_r = 3, so the clamp set its target; see the observation for the venue-side read that established it. ⚠️ AND NOTE THE ELIGIBLE POPULATION IS THREE LEGS, NOT TEN: read against the live /api/bot/config on 2026-09-01, only trend_donchian_xrp_4h (3), ada_pullback_2h (4) and xrp_pullback_2h (3.0) carry a changed tp_r; the other seven still hold the tp_r: 50 sentinel, where the clamp is the only thing setting a target and no trade can EVER satisfy this clause. What half (b) now owes is a trade on one of those three whose risk is under 0.099/tp_r of entry. ⚠️ THE STOP HALF IS NOT RE-OWED: atr_stop_mult=2 is already verified end to end on real money against broker truth by trade 5250 (declared 1.38875714, venue fill 1.3888, one tick), and this sharpening does not reopen it.
items.why_it_cannot_be_closed_by_time: Nothing about waiting makes a config value reach a process or a trade close under it. The 4h legs open rarely, so the soak can look identical to a broken deploy for days — which is exactly the state this row distinguishes.

probe.checks: HALF (b) ONLY — the half this row still owes. Half (a) is already recorded SATISFIED in the observation (all eleven field values read back from the live /api/bot/config on 2026-08-30, with /api/diag/version showing git_sha 892c9a2c), so re-probing it would test a settled question. This looks for a CLOSED trade that is real-money, on one of the nine shipped e35 legs, whose pnlProvenance is measured or estimated (clears_when explicitly rules out fabricated and unverified), and — the word clears_when calls 'the whole criterion' — OPENED AFTER the deploy rather than merely closed after it. The boundary 2026-08-30T14:05:00+00:00 is not the commit time: it is the instant the observation records half (a) as MEASURED true on the running trader, so a matching trade demonstrably opened under config confirmed live. It is conservative by construction — it may exclude a qualifying trade opened slightly earlier, which errs toward under-reporting, the safe direction for a criterion that must not be cleared spuriously. `openedAt` is compared lexicographically, which is chronological ONLY because the route serves a +00:00 offset (measured); a switch to a 'Z' suffix would silently break it, and the positive control is what would catch that. The control is the leg-name set itself, matching 40 of 200 rows on 2026-08-31 — so a renamed leg turns this into could_not_look rather than a permanent quiet negative.
probe.is_not: A pass does NOT establish that the trade was closed BY THE STRATEGY. clears_when forbids grading the exit off exit_reason alone, and the row's own near-miss is the proof: trade 4904 read 'reconciler_filled' for what was an OPERATOR FLATTEN. No field on this route separates a strategy exit from an operator action, so that judgement stays a session's. Nor does a pass establish BROKER TRUTH, which clears_when asks for: pnlProvenance grades how THIS ROW's number was derived, while journalTrust grades whether the ACCOUNT reconciles with the venue wallet at all, and they are different questions — a 'measured' row on a 'known_divergent' account is exactly that gap, and bybit_2 is such an account. Finally it cannot tell whether the trade exercised the CHANGED geometry: a trade on ada_pullback_2h or trend_donchian_xrp_4h that closed on its stop says nothing about the tp_r 50->3/4 change those two legs received, which is the part of the ship the row most wants looked at. items.summary: The live Bybit wallet-truth path works and is MEASURED, but it does not and cannot currently reproduce the -$262.52 figure it was built to replace -- the two are over almost disjoint windows. Switching journalTrust over is therefore NOT a one-line flip, and the decision is open.
items.observation:
First live pull 2026-08-31T08:43:52Z (issue #10565): days=60 chunks=9, 2789 rows inserted (bybit_1 1821 / bybit_2 618 / bybit_portfolio 350). The chunk count is the proof the deep window is WALKED rather than asked for in one call -- 9 chunks of <=7 days, against Bybit V5's 7-day range cap. ACTION_DAYS forwarded correctly (days=60, not the wrapper's 7 default).

/api/diag/bybit_wallet_truth reads all three accounts `measured_api`. bybit_2: +$17.04 over 2026-07-02 -> 2026-08-31 (60d, 618 rows); +$32.66 over the route's 30d default. The LEDGER says -$262.52 over 2026-04-15 -> 2026-07-13 (comms/broker_truth_ledger.json, source bybit_um_export_stitched).

THE WINDOWS OVERLAP BY ELEVEN DAYS (07-02..07-13). +$17.04 neither confirms nor contradicts -$262.52; they measure different populations. The cross-check I set out to perform COULD NOT BE PERFORMED, and saying so is the finding. || 2026-08-31 (session_01P2QBKN): DECIDED — (b), AND THE ROW'S STATED REASON FOR IT IS REFUTED. Ran the deep pull the clears_when demanded (pull-bybit-transaction-log days=150, issue #10609, run 33419842621: 22 chunks x 3 accounts, bybit_2 fetched 646 / inserted 27). RETENTION IS NOT THE CONSTRAINT: asking back to 2025-07-27 (days=400) returns EXACTLY the same 631 rows as asking back to 2026-04-15 (days=138), and the earliest row sits between 2026-04-18 and 2026-04-23 — bracketed by shrinking the window until the count fell 631 -> 629, because the route reports the window ASKED FOR and never the data's own span. So the row's hypothesis (a) 'a deeper pull reproduces the lifetime figure' is dead, and its hypothesis (b) 'retention does not reach' is ALSO wrong about the cause. THE ACTUAL CAUSE, exact to the cent: over the ledger's own window this path returns -1.52 (by subtraction: full 2026-04-18->08-31 = +9.76 over 631 rows, minus post-ledger 2026-07-13->08-31 = +11.29 over 476 rows). The ledger's own note reads 'stitched across two sub-accounts (MAIN -1.52 + SUB -261.01)'. So the live path reproduces MAIN EXACTLY and cannot see SUB at all — the account switched sub-accounts on 2026-05-10. It is a SUB-ACCOUNT SCOPE limit, not a window limit, and NO `days` value can close it. ⚠️ CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CONTRACT: documenting realized_usd as 'windowed' would tell a reader a wider window completes it. It does not. The honest label is 'this sub-account only'. Documented on src/runtime/bybit_wallet_truth.py. ⚠️ AND THE REASON NOT TO SWITCH IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN CAUTIONARY: the ledger's -262.52 is what marks bybit_2 (REAL MONEY) `known_divergent`; this path returns -1.52, which sits beside the journal's own ~-33 and would make the account read as broadly reconciled — retiring a real divergence flag while missing -261.01 of it. The ledger STAYS as the lifetime record. Switching needs a sub-account join, which is new work and not a flip.
items.detail:
Reproducing the ledger needs a pull covering 2026-04-15 -> 2026-07-13, i.e. ~138 days back from today. WHETHER BYBIT'S TRANSACTION-LOG RETENTION REACHES THAT FAR IS UNKNOWN and is testable with one deeper pull (the puller is idempotent, so re-running at days=150 costs nothing but API calls).

This VALIDATES the decision in PR #10532 to leave journalTrust reading the frozen ledger rather than switching it in the same change. It also changes what the switch means: either (a) a deeper pull reproduces the lifetime figure and the ledger is retired, or (b) retention does not reach and the live figure is a WINDOWED realized that consumers must read as such -- not a drop-in replacement for a lifetime cumulative. Those are different contracts and the choice is the operator's.
items.clears_when: The sub-account join is solved — the live path can see BOTH sub-accounts for bybit_2 and reproduces the stitched figure — OR the operator records that bybit_2's lifetime truth stays hand-maintained permanently. ⚠️ SUPERSEDES the original clears_when, whose (a)/(b) both rested on a retention question that has now been ANSWERED and was the wrong question: retention reaches, the scope does not. Re-running the puller at any `days` value does NOT clear this.

It also cannot distinguish a genuine infeasible grade from a hand-edited or backfilled row. Read the matching row and confirm its provenance before clearing. A FAIL is likewise not evidence that the state is unreachable: clears_when's own escape hatch — that if no queue unit can ever be graded infeasible the honest close is to retire the state or the row — is a judgement no probe makes.

items.summary: The research queue's GPU route and its spend-gate preflight have NEVER been exercised. Do not describe the GPU spend gates as verified.
items.observation:
CARRIED FORWARD from OI-20260827-RESEARCH-QUEUE-DISPATCHER-NEVER-FIRED, which was CLEARED on 2026-08-31. That row's two criteria were met and are recorded below; this row exists so the one caveat inside it does not vanish with it — clearing a row must not delete the knowledge it held.

WHAT CLEARED, with evidence read rather than inferred:
(a) A SCHEDULED dispatcher run dispatched a real job and its rows landed in the store the job declares. Run 33340458710 (event=schedule, 2026-08-30T22:56:22Z) logged `RQ-20260827-001 dispatched gld-compat-matrix.yml on main (route=runner)`, and docs/research/gld-compat-matrix-verdicts.jsonl on main carries 11 rows at run_generated_at=2026-08-30T22:56:50Z — 28 seconds later. Verified by READING the store, not by a workflow exit code. The next scheduled run repeats it at 23:34:31Z.
(b) The cadence stamp race was exercised. RQ-20260830-002 (cadence: monthly) fired at 12:29:28Z; on the NEXT dispatcher run the same job logged `not_due — last ran 2026-08-30T12:29:28+00:00, cadence monthly not yet elapsed`.

⚠️ THE CLEARED ROW ALSO SAID 'its cron has never fired', AND THAT WAS STALE — 5 of 8 dispatcher runs carry event=schedule. It understated progress while, separately, hiding a real regression: the two most recent SCHEDULED runs both FAILED, on BL-20260830-A-TRANSIENT-RED-BASE-PERMANENTLY-STRANDS-AN-AUTOMERGE-BRANCH (the dispatch itself succeeded; the stamp PR never merged). That failure is tracked on the backlog row, not here.

WHAT IS UNPROVEN AND IS THIS ROW'S SUBJECT: the queue has never held a GPU-routed job, so the ledger preflight has never been observed either refusing or admitting a run. Nothing about the runner route is evidence about the GPU route — different branch, different gate, real money.
items.clears_when: A GPU-routed job is fired once and the ledger preflight is OBSERVED making a decision — either refusing the run on budget or admitting it — read from that run's own output, not from a test or a dry run. Both outcomes clear it; what does not clear it is a GPU job that never reached the preflight, or a runner-routed job however many times it succeeds.

probe.checks: Looks for a gpu-burst-train.yml run whose logs carry the preflight step at all, over the last 20 runs. ⚠️ THE REASON THIS ROW CARRIED FOR HAVING NO PROBE WAS A CATEGORY ERROR, which is why it now has one: it said a scheduled probe 'cannot produce that without FIRING a GPU job, which spends real budget'. True about FIRING and irrelevant to PROBING — NO probe in this family produces the event it watches (pairs_soak does not open a pair; arbitration_fanout_soak does not route an order). Conflating producing an observation with observing it turned a buildable probe into a declared impossibility. This fires no job, spends nothing, and only reads.
probe.is_not: ⚠️ A PASS HERE IS THE WEAKEST IN THE FAMILY AND MUST NOT CLEAR THE ROW ON ITS OWN. clears_when demands the preflight be OBSERVED MAKING A DECISION — refusing on budget or admitting — and explicitly rules out a dry run. This cannot separate those: with GPU_BURST_ARMED != 1 the workflow runs a DRY PREFLIGHT ONLY, and its log carries the same step name as an armed run. So a pass means 'a run exists that reached the preflight step', and a session must read that run's own output to see whether it was armed and what it decided. The literal is deliberately the step name rather than a decision string, because no decision string has ever been observed in a real run — inventing one would be a predicate matching nothing while looking precise. Tighten it to the real decision line the first time an armed run happens. Since the event never occurs spontaneously, a FAIL here means 'nobody has fired one', not 'the gate is broken'.

items.summary: session-brief-guard is diff-scoped now, so a brief that goes stale on the CLOCK can no longer fail a PR that did not touch the registers. The `inherited` verdict has NEVER been emitted by a real CI run — it is deployed, not proven.
items.observation:
WHY THIS EXISTS. `render_session_brief` calls `datetime.now()` and `due_items` flips a monitoring row to DUE once `check_every_days` elapses, so the block COMMITTED in CLAUDE.md goes stale at a UTC-midnight boundary with no commit anywhere. The whole-tree `--check` then reds EVERY open PR until a human re-renders, and nothing re-runs a branch's checks, so a branch cut inside that window is stranded permanently.

MEASURED 2026-08-31, not inferred: OI-20260826-MHG-OVER-COVER-MECHANISM-UNVERIFIED (verified_at 2026-08-29, check_every_days 2) crossed into DUE at 00:00Z. PRs #10538 (00:47Z) and #10539 (01:22Z) BOTH failed on exactly `session-brief-guard` — read from the job logs, not guessed — with pytest-run, pytest-collect and repo-inventory GREEN on both. CLAUDE.md was not re-rendered until 06:47Z. Merging current main into each branch (operator-approved) turned `guards` GREEN on both with no content change, which is the positive control that the cause was the clock and not their rows.

STATE THE POPULATION: 2 of the 3 stranded automation PRs were inspected. #10398 was NOT examined (operator said do not touch it), so it is NOT claimed to share this cause.

WHAT IS NOT YET PROVEN: every test of the fix is synthetic — a temp git repo built by tests/test_session_brief_diff_scope.py. No REAL CI run has printed `verdict=inherited`, which is the only evidence the diff-scoped path behaves on a live PR (a `--base origin/main` that cannot resolve in the guards job would grade `base_unreadable` and FAIL CLOSED — the same red as before, for a different reason, which is exactly the confusion this row exists to catch). The one-shot `commit-to-main` refresh is likewise unexercised: no run has reported a `stale-branch refresh -> ...` notice.

=== 2026-08-31, HALF (a) STILL OPEN; THE FINDING CLAUSE IS RULED OUT. ===
The diff-scoped guard ran in real CI twice on PR #10575 (`guards` green on both 00cfb57e and
d4f4c745, with `--check --base origin/main`). It printed `clean`, NOT `inherited` — the brief
was current on both sides, so half (a) is genuinely unmet rather than quietly satisfied.
⚠️ But the FINDING this row names — `verdict=base_unreadable`, i.e. origin/main not resolving
in the guards job — DID NOT OCCUR. That was the specific risk of shipping a ref-dependent
check, and it is now ruled out by observation rather than by reasoning.
Half (b) also unmet, correctly: the dispatcher's stamp PR (#10576) merged without stalling,
so the one-shot refresh had nothing to do and printed no `stale-branch refresh ->` line.
Neither half can be forced; both need a PR that opens across a cadence boundary.
items.clears_when: BOTH: (a) a real CI run prints `session-brief: verdict=inherited` on a PR that did not touch the registers, found in that run's job log rather than reasoned about; and (b) a `commit-to-main` run prints `stale-branch refresh -> refreshed` or `-> not_needed_up_to_date`, proving the branch is on the new code path at all. A passing synthetic test is NEITHER half. If instead a run prints `verdict=base_unreadable`, that is a FINDING — `origin/main` is not resolvable in the guards job — and the fix is the ref, not this row.

probe.checks: BOTH halves, in the two DIFFERENT workflows that print them, because clears_when requires both and a pass on one half is the over-read this family exists to prevent. (a) `session-brief: verdict=inherited` in a guards.yml run — emitted only by render_session_brief.py's inherited branch, so its presence IS the diff-scoping path having been taken on a real PR. (b) `commit-to-main: stale-branch refresh ->` in a due-list.yml run — the composite action prints it with the resulting state, proving the automation branch is on the new code path at all. Each group is scanned over the last 20 runs and EVERY group must hit. The positive control `session-brief:` appears in essentially every guards run, so a workflow rename, an expired log or a revoked token becomes could_not_look instead of a permanent quiet negative.
probe.is_not: A pass does NOT establish that half (a) came from a PR that genuinely did not touch the registers — the log line does not carry the diff, and `inherited` is explicitly NOT 'the brief is fine', it is 'this PR did not break it'. Nor does it tell which of `-> refreshed` and `-> not_needed_up_to_date` half (b) printed; clears_when accepts either, but they mean different things and a session grading the mechanism should read which. ⚠️ THIS READER HAS NEVER RUN AGAINST THE REAL ACTIONS API: api.github.com is intercepted at HTTP 403 from a Claude Code on the web sandbox, so its controls run against a fake server and its FIRST scheduled run is its real verification. That is safe only because a broken reader here reports could_not_run, never fail — if this row shows could_not_run after the probes workflow has run, suspect the reader before the mechanism. Finally, clears_when's own escape hatch stands: a run printing `verdict=base_unreadable` is a FINDING about the ref, not evidence for this row, and no probe makes that call.

items.summary: scope-overlap-audit works — its FIRST GENUINE catch landed 2026-08-31T17:26Z. But the same comment ALSO reported this session's own board START back at it, because the attributor compares the START's branch to the PR's branch and a session posts ONE START while opening PRs from SEVERAL branches. Read an overlap comment expecting one line of it to be yours.
items.clears_when: A scope-overlap comment on a PR from a session that posted its START under a DIFFERENT branch name lists that START under the `mine` attribution (i.e. it is NOT rendered as another session's) — read from the comment body. The proposed fix is a session-suffix match; any fix that achieves the above clears this.
items.observation: MEASURED 2026-08-31T17:26:46Z on PR #10607, read from the posted comment, not from the code. It reported `Compared 3 changed file(s) against 66 declared path(s) — 6 attributed to another session, 2 unattributable`. THE GENUINE HALF IS REAL AND IS THE FIRST ONE: `claude/research-queue-landing-v4yfq7` (11:41Z, 15:24Z) and `claude/research-disposition-resweep-cplgnv` (15:55Z) had both declared `docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json`, and the latter also `ROADMAP.md` and `docs/sprint-logs/` — all three files this PR changes. That supersedes any claim that the detector has never caught a real overlap; it has. THE DEFECT IS THE THIRD LINE: `claude/workflows-audit-restructure-fz0sw9` is THIS session's own designated branch, and the PR was opened from `claude/session-wrapup-fz0sw9`, so `attribution()`'s `branch == my_branch` test graded the session's own START as `other`. This is the SAME false-positive class fixed in #10594, in a narrower form — that fix handled a START with no branch; this is a START with a DIFFERENT branch from the same session. It is the COMMON shape, not an edge case: a session posts one START and opens per-task branches. PROPOSED FIX (small, not applied here): the trailing 6-char session suffix is shared across a session's branches (`fz0sw9`, `v4yfq7`, `cplgnv`), so match on that suffix in addition to the exact branch. It must ADD to `mine`, never suppress an `other` — under-reporting a real overlap is the worse error, which is why the `unattributable` state already resolves toward reporting. ⚠️ NOT A BLOCKER FOR #10607: the overlap was verified harmless — those sessions' work had already merged (#10602, #10604) and `git merge-tree` against `origin/main` was CLEAN.

items.summary: render_due_list now grades the probe report's AGE against the cadence parsed from probes.yml, emitting PROBE-REPORT-STALE / PROBE-REPORT-UNDATEABLE / PROBE-CADENCE-UNKNOWN. Live it has only ever read `fresh`. The three non-fresh verdicts are deployed and have never been emitted by a real run.
items.clears_when: A real `render_due_list` run emits one of PROBE-REPORT-STALE, PROBE-REPORT-UNDATEABLE or PROBE-CADENCE-UNKNOWN and the emitted row's stamped `[observed <ts>, <age> ago]` matches the probe report actually on disk. A self-test pass is NOT this — the 26 self-test cases already cover all three.
items.observation: MEASURED 2026-08-31 against the real repo: `freshness=fresh age=3.6h cadence=daily (cron 20 5 * * *)`. That is the only state a live run has produced. WHY THE OTHER THREE MATTER MORE THAN `fresh`: a due-list that silently serves a probe report from a week ago reads exactly like one serving today's, which is the whole failure this grading exists to end — `we did not look` must stay distinct from `we looked and found nothing`. `undateable` deliberately resolves toward REPORTING rather than silence: a report that cannot be dated cannot be shown to be current. `_PROBE_STALE_SLACK_H` is 6.0, a CHOSEN value with no distribution behind it.

items.summary: Whether the half-built local LLM carries any weight is UNDECIDED — and it is undecided BY THE OPERATOR, not for want of evidence. ⚠️ THIS SUMMARY PREVIOUSLY ENDED '#10605 makes that arm dispatchable via LLMBENCH_MODEL_URL; it has NOT been run' — that was true when written and became FALSE on 2026-09-01, in the dangerous direction: a session reading only the summary would conclude the measurement is still owed and re-run a 16-minute job on the 1-core trainer under the heavy lock. BOTH SIZE ARMS ARE NOW MEASURED ON ANSWER QUALITY. 1.5B: fabricated a causal claim and misattributed the fault. 3B (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct Q4_K_M, `RESULT: benchmarked`, `single-shot flag: -st`, both controls passing): better on BOTH of those specific defects — it hedges instead of inventing, and keeps the fault on the internal side — but never names the mechanism, at ~2.1x the latency and ~0.96 GB of headroom. So the REMAINING step is the operator's decision, which is the last clause of clears_when ('Then the operator decides'). Read the observation for the full sample and for one correction it carries: the truncation both models show is OURS (`-n 200`), not evidence about either model.
items.clears_when: A `llm_capacity_benchmark.sh` run under LLMBENCH_MODEL_URL reaches `RESULT: benchmarked` with `model:` naming the requested URL and NO `requested override did NOT serve` warning, and its generation sample is compared against the 1.5B baseline below on ANSWER QUALITY against the same real repo question. Then the operator decides. A throughput comparison alone does NOT clear this.
items.observation:
MEASURED 2026-08-31 on the trainer VM, post-reboot, RESULT: benchmarked, flag probe selected `--single-turn`. Throughput pp128 22.35 +/- 0.24, tg64 7.19 +/- 0.34 t/s (pre-reboot 22.53 / 7.38 — identical within noise). 36.4s wall, 2.86 GB peak RSS on a 5.9 GB box. THE QUALITY IS THE FINDING, NOT THE SPEED: the sample restated the prompt, FABRICATED a causal claim ('margin was calculated from the per-coin block, indicating that the available balance is less than the required margin' — two unrelated facts joined by an invented 'indicating'), MISATTRIBUTED the fault to venue liquidity when the defect was our own sizer reading an empty account-level field, and TRUNCATED mid-sentence without answering the third of the prompt asking what to check next. A model that confidently invents a cause is worse than no model on a system whose canonical rule is always-verify. THE SIZE EXPECTATION IS ARITHMETIC, NOT A MEASUREMENT — a 3B roughly halves the speed and should raise quality, a 0.5B does the reverse; do not quote either as a result. || 2026-08-31, session ayloee — THE DIFFERENT-SIZE ARM WAS RUN AND THIS ROW DOES NOT CLEAR, BY ITS OWN CRITERION. clears_when says in as many words that a throughput comparison alone does NOT clear it, and a throughput comparison is exactly what came back. Dispatched via LLMBENCH_MODEL_URL (issue #10621) with a dispatch-time positive control; `model:` named the requested Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct Q4_K_M URL with NO fallback warning, so the arm is genuine. MEASURED: pp128 10.57 +/- 0.04, tg64 3.91 +/- 0.00 t/s, peak RSS 4,792,340 KB = 4.79 GB on the 5.9 GB box — 2.1x and 1.84x slower than the 1.5B, fitting with ~1.1 GB headroom. NOT MEASURED: the answer. RESULT was `benchmarked_throughput_only`, exit status 124 (timeout), 15:01.52 wall clock, and the captured output is fourteen `>` prompts then `Exiting...` — llama-cli sat in interactive mode and never generated. So nothing whatever may be concluded about 3B answer quality: not 'similar to the 1.5B', not 'presumably worse'. CAUSE, root-caused after two of my own explanations were refuted by measurement (the flag candidate list is NOT stale — `-st` and `--single-turn` are both in build e4b9af0's 562-line help; `--help` does NOT exit non-zero — it exits 0): SIGPIPE. `grep -q` exits on first match, closing the pipe while llama-cli is still writing; llama-cli dies 141 and the script's own `set -uo pipefail` makes the pipeline report 141, so the `if` was FALSE though grep had MATCHED. Measured all three arms (no-pipefail rc=0 / pipefail SKIPPED rc=141 / control TAKEN). Fixed by capturing --help once and matching with `case`. ⚠️ THIS IS THE THREE-STATE CONTRACT WORKING, NOT FAILING: #10597 exists so `benchmarked` is never printed over a generation step that did not run, and it was not — the run graded itself and named which half is valid. OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-31: RE-RUN for the answer. It is queued against main once the SIGPIPE fix lands (PR #10620) and costs a full llama.cpp rebuild plus a 2 GB re-download on the 1-core trainer under the heavy lock — the EXIT trap cleaned up, disk back to 7.4 G. || 2026-09-01 (session 01HYXKHpDQeWv3u4rjWWoL2J): THE RE-RUN COMPLETED AND THE ANSWER IS NOW MEASURED — the row is READY FOR THE OPERATOR'S DECISION and is NOT cleared by me, because clears_when ends 'Then the operator decides.' Collected via trainer-diag #10642 off the run launched 2026-08-31T22:11:17Z, finished 22:27:49Z. BOTH CONTROLS PASS, which is what makes the sample gradeable at all: `single-shot flag: -st` (the SIGPIPE fix in #10620 works — the previous run's `benchmarked_throughput_only` is gone) and `RESULT: benchmarked`. DONE marker present, no process running, lock released, EXIT trap cleaned up (disk 7.4G). Throughput on the real generation path: pp128 9.67 +/- 1.27, tg64 3.91 +/- 0.00 t/s; end-to-end 10.5 t/s prompt / 3.7 t/s generation; 200 tokens in 71.07s wall at 96% CPU; peak RSS 4,947,364 KB = 4.95 GB on the 5.9 GB box, ~0.96 GB headroom. Consistent with the earlier throughput-only arm (10.57 / 3.91), so the speed answer has not moved: ~2.1x and ~1.84x slower than the 1.5B.

THE ANSWER, WHICH IS THE DELIVERABLE. Same prompt as the 1.5B baseline. THE 3B IS BETTER ON BOTH SPECIFIC DEFECTS THE 1.5B WAS FAILED FOR, and that is a real improvement rather than a hedge: (1) NO FABRICATED CAUSAL CLAIM — where the 1.5B joined two unrelated facts with an invented 'indicating', the 3B hedges correctly ('This suggests a discrepancy', 'could indicate issues with the margin calculation process'); (2) NO MISATTRIBUTION — the 1.5B blamed venue liquidity, while the 3B keeps the fault on the internal side ('the margin calculation process', 'the margin management system'), which is where the defect actually was. ⚠️ BUT IT NEVER NAMES THE MECHANISM. The real cause is that the sizer fell back to TOTAL EQUITY and counted initial margin already pledged to open positions as free (BL-20260813-ICTSCALP-BTC-BYBIT2-BALANCE-REJECTS, fixed by the coin_derived rung). The 3B produces generic-competent prose that restates the prompt and gestures at 'a discrepancy' — nothing a session could act on. ⚠️ AND CORRECT ONE THING IN THE BASELINE ABOVE: it attributes the 1.5B's truncation to the model ('TRUNCATED mid-sentence without answering the third of the prompt asking what to check next'). THE 3B TRUNCATES AT THE SAME PLACE — 3 complete bullets then a severed '- **Next Steps to' — and the cause is OURS, not the model's: the harness passes `-n 200`, a generation cap both runs hit. Truncation is therefore NOT evidence about either model and must not be counted against the 3B or re-quoted against the 1.5B; raising `-n` is the fix if the 'what to check next' third is ever to be graded.

SO THE MEASURED VERDICT IS: better where it was failed, still not useful, at ~2x the cost and ~1 GB of headroom on a 1-core box. My reading is that this does not carry weight for analysis work on a system whose canonical rule is always-verify — plausible generic prose is the failure mode that rule exists to catch — but the decision is the operator's and the row stays open for it.

items.summary: The research pipeline's MACHINERY is healthy and its READING is in debt. Measured 2026-08-31T21:0xZ via research_disposition.survey(): 370 units across 3 corpora — 103 dispositioned, 11 UNREAD (live), 256 superseded_unread. The queue itself is idle BY DESIGN (all 5 jobs `not_due`: 2 done, 1 cadence=once already ran, 2 monthly not elapsed), so nothing is stuck — the debt is that output arrives faster than anyone reads it.
items.detail: THE 11 UNREAD ARE ALL gld_compat, ALL FROM ONE RUN at 2026-08-31T17:20:54Z — one unit per account (alpaca_live, alpaca_options_paper, alpaca_paper, alpaca_portfolio, breakout_1, bybit_1, bybit_2, bybit_portfolio, ib_live, ib_paper, oanda_practice). ⚠️ These are GRADEABLE BY READING, not by waiting: N_FIELD['gld_compat'] is None because the job is DETERMINISTIC, so the R4 power gate correctly declines and `n_oos: null` means 'no sample size APPLIES', never 'we failed to read one'. Nothing will make them readier. ⚠️ AND THE 'unread 0' FIGURE IN BL-20260831-SUPERSEDED-UNREAD-IS-256-AND-NOBODY-HAS-ESTABLISHED-HOW-MUCH-OF-IT-IS-BENIGN IS NOW STALE — it was true when written and this run landed after it. LEDGER: 117 entries — 53 terminal (1 actioned, 52 no_action_warranted), 64 underpowered. ⚠️ UNRECONCILED: 103 units in `dispositioned` state against 117 ledger entries, a 14-row gap. It is PROBABLY units dispositioned and later superseded; that was NOT verified and neither figure should be quoted as throughput until it is.

items.detail:
WHAT CHANGED. alpaca_live sat at mode: live with strategies: [] since 2026-08-29, and that empty list was the ENTIRE gate — there is no mode flip behind it, so adding this leg IS the live-trading moment. Two coordinated changes, both operator-approved in conversation: (Tier-2) ALPACA_CASH_SETTLEMENT_MODE=apply scoped by ALPACA_CASH_SETTLEMENT_ACCOUNTS=alpaca_live, armed FIRST so the T+1 gate binds before the first order, verified on /proc/<MainPID>/environ via get-env #10631/#10632; (Tier-3) strategies [] -> [tlt_pullback_1h].

WHY THIS LEG, and it is NOT an edge claim. Measured 2026-08-31 over trade_journal.db::order_packages (filter_state: applied asserted — that route IGNORES an unknown filter column and silently returns the whole table, which is how a first pass of this same measurement produced five identical wrong numbers): tlt_pullback_1h has n=74 packages 2026-06-22->2026-08-28, 33 of them long (44.6%), against ≤7 packages for every other affordable long-capable leg on the roster, and gdx_pullback_1d at 0 long of 7. It is execution: live with no strategy-level side_filter, and TLT is in the account's symbols. The ROSTER INTENT is a PLUMBING TEST — prove fills reconcile against exchange truth, that whole-share sizing behaves on a cash book, that silent_refusal_alert grades the account healthy — and stripped of uso_trend_1h (excluded on standing non-financial grounds) the candidate set has NO positive measured record on either paper population. Do not report a first fill as evidence of edge.

WHAT TO EXPECT, so a normal state is not misread as a fault. (a) Roughly HALF this leg's signals will be journalled as suppressed would-be trades: side_filter: long is declared, and independently this is a CASH account with shorting_enabled: false, so the short 55.4% of its flow is structurally unexecutable. (b) The sizer will demand ~11x the account (4.70x median exposure multiple at risk_pct 0.02) and the 0.9 cash wall will clamp it to 2 shares (~$165 of $200.10), so realised risk at the declared stop is ~$0.75 rather than the $4.00 the 2% implies. Neither is a bug; both are the design.

HOW TO CHECK (transferred off a session-bound timer 2026-09-01 at operator direction — this row is now the ONLY carrier, so it must be runnable cold). (1) /api/bot/db/table/trades?filter_col=account_id&filter_op=eq&filter_val=alpaca_live&limit=50&order_by=id&order_dir=desc — ⚠️ ASSERT filter_state == 'applied' BEFORE trusting any count; an unknown filter column is silently IGNORED and returns the WHOLE table, a trap that already produced five identical wrong numbers in this lane. BASELINE at 2026-09-01T14:20Z: total 335, newest 2026-08-28T19:00:38Z, 0 non-rejected. (2) If total is UNCHANGED, cross-check order_packages?filter_col=strategy_name&filter_op=eq&filter_val=tlt_pullback_1h (baseline total 74, newest 2026-08-28T17:18:14) — if THAT moved while alpaca_live got no row, the leg is being dropped and THAT IS THE FINDING; if neither moved, the leg simply has not signalled and nothing is wrong. (3) Control that the pipeline is alive at all: newest order_packages row overall, any strategy. (4) /api/diag/log_file?name=cash_settlement_soak — the first alpaca_live row there is itself evidence the T+1 gate is finally exercised on a real account (it has never produced one). (5) /api/diag/log_file?name=silent_refusal_alert_state — ⚠️ this account is on SILENT_REFUSAL_SKIP, so its entry is FROZEN and CANNOT update; do not read it as a clean bill of health (BL-20260823-ALPACA-LIVE-IS-EXEMPT-FROM-BOTH-DETECTORS-THAT-WATCH-IT). WHAT WOULD BE A REAL FAULT: a refusal whose cause is NOT the side filter and NOT the cash clamp — in particular a venue rejection, an unreadable balance (BL-20260813-ALPACA-BALANCE-NONE-WHILE-ACCOUNT-READS-ACTIVE), or a fill that does not reconcile against exchange truth.
items.clears_when: alpaca_live has PLACED at least one real order for tlt_pullback_1h and the outcome has been read back from exchange truth — either a fill that reconciles, or a refusal whose logged cause is understood and is not the expected side-filter/cash-clamp path. A journalled would-be trade is NOT a placement. A soak row is NOT a placement. Read trade_journal.db::trades for account_id=alpaca_live with a status other than 'rejected'. ⚠️ EXTENDED BY OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-08-31 (end-of-day wrap): the bar is a COMPLETE ROUND TRIP — ONE ENTRY AND ITS EXIT — not merely a first fill. An entry alone proves only half the plumbing this leg exists to test: it shows an order can reach the venue, and says nothing about whether the exit path works on a CASH book, whether the close reconciles against exchange truth, or whether T+1 then binds the NEXT buy — which is the whole reason the settlement gate was armed first. BOTH must be observed: (a) a trades row for account_id=alpaca_live with status other than 'rejected', AND (b) that same row reaching status='closed' with an exit whose pnlProvenance is measured or estimated, NOT fabricated or unverified. ⚠️ TRANSCRIPTION CAVEAT, flagged rather than silently resolved: the directive arrived by voice as "one trim and one string", which is garbled. It is read here as ONE TRADE, ENTRY AND EXIT. If a different thing was meant — e.g. one entry and one STOP, or one trade per SYMBOL — correct this row rather than working around it.
items.why_it_cannot_be_closed_by_time: The leg signals roughly every 2.4 days on its long side, so a week of silence is weak evidence either way and MUST NOT be read as 'it works'. Nothing accrues that proves the account can trade; only an order does. This account previously spent 16 days emitting 120 refusals with nothing alerting (BL-20260821-ALPACA-LIVE-REFUSES-EVERY-ORDER-127-OF-127), which is exactly the silence this row exists to stop repeating.
items.probe_absent_reason: NOT because the condition is unprobeable — it is machine-checkable and the data is reachable — but because `probe_soak.py` CANNOT READ THE ONE ENDPOINT THAT CARRIES IT, and fails in the dangerous direction. Measured 2026-08-31: /api/diag/journal?table=trades&limit=1000 returns a BARE LIST, not an envelope, so fetch_rows raises AttributeError at `payload.get(key)` (probe_soak.py:149) before reaching its own correct `unrecognised envelope -> could-not-look` branch four lines below. The unhandled traceback exits 1, and 1 is EXIT_FAIL — 'the log was READ and NOTHING matched'. That is precisely the confusion the module's docstring exists to prevent ('the payload was not the expected envelope' is listed under code 2, emphatically NOT code 1), and it is invisible here because `fail` is ALREADY this row's expected state, so a crash and the truth render identically. Declaring a probe today would register a permanent false negative on a REAL-MONEY row. The predicate itself is sound and was checked by hand: that tail spans 2026-07-31->2026-08-31 and holds 80 alpaca_live rows (a real denominator, not zero), all `rejected`, so `account_id=alpaca_live` + `status~open,closed,filled` reads FAIL correctly today and would flip to PASS on the first placement. Filed as BL-20260831-PROBE-SOAK-CRASHES-ON-A-BARE-LIST-PAYLOAD-AND-REPORTS-IT-AS-A-REAL-NEGATIVE; register the probe once that lands. The 3 existing probes all read /api/diag/log_file envelopes and are unaffected.
