items.summary: Operating-layer PHASE H (the control half) shipped the DECISION ROUND-TRIP as a draft PR (#10705 bot, ict-trader-dashboard#211 SPA): a work object may declare answerable `decision_requests[]`, `GET /api/bot/work/decisions` is the inbox, `POST /api/bot/work/decision` submits an answer (token-gated, FAIL-CLOSED), and `scripts/ops/commit_work_decisions.py` + `.github/workflows/work-decision-commit.yml` commit it into the repo. ⚠️ NOT ONE DECISION HAS MADE THE ROUND-TRIP, and every stage of it is independently unproven on the fleet: (a) the routes are NOT DEPLOYED (draft PR); (b) `DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN` is UNSET on the live web-api as far as this session could establish, so the write route would serve 503 and `writeGate.state` reads `closed_no_token` — whether to set it is an OPERATOR decision, not a bug; (c) the SPA panel has never been RENDERED (this session cannot render the deployed page, the same limit `WO-20260901-PHASE-B` held an edge open for); (d) the committer workflow's SSH+curl step has NEVER RUN — it is proven by shape, copied from `vm-diag-snapshot.yml`, not by a run, and this repo has scheduled workflows that are merged, enabled, correct and fire LATE and ERRATICALLY rather than on their declared cadence -- CORRECTED 2026-09-02: probes.yml HAS now fired on cron (actions_list on probes.yml, event=schedule, total_count 1, run #34, conclusion success, 2026-09-01T10:12:17Z) and that row is CLEARED. The caution it carried still stands and is now better evidenced, not weaker: its cron is `20 5 * * *` and it fired at 10:12Z, roughly 4h50m LATE, and once rather than daily. So correct cron syntax still is not evidence of a run -- read the run history). ⚠️ THE RISK THIS ROW WATCHES IS NOT THAT THE CODE IS WRONG. It is that a decision channel with a question in it and no round-trip behind it is WORSE than no channel: the operator answers, nothing lands, and the question reads `in_transit` forever while looking like it was dealt with. The design's own words are that visibility is the enforcement mechanism this system has never had — a channel that swallows answers is anti-enforcement. ⚠️ THERE IS EXACTLY ONE REAL QUESTION IN IT TODAY: `DEC-20260901-READ-GATE-SEQUENCING` on `WO-20260901-PHASE-H`, and it BLOCKS the other half of Phase H (the read gate), which was deliberately not built because its own precondition — Streamlit + Android off the live feed — is unmet. Measured before it existed: of 584 objects, ZERO declared a `decision_requests` block and ZERO carried an `operator_decision` edge. `verified_at` is deliberately null: no observation has been made, and dating it today would be a claim of one.
items.clears_when: ONE decision completes the FULL round-trip and is observed doing it, end to end: an answer submitted from the deployed SPA appears on `/api/bot/work/decisions` as `in_transit`, and then a LATER read of the same route grades that same request `committed` with the `answer` block visible in `docs/claude/work/objects/<id>.yaml` on `main`. Record WHICH request and WHO answered it. ⚠️ MERGING THE TWO PRs DOES NOT CLEAR THIS — a merge is not a deploy, and a deploy is not an answer. That distinction is why `BL-20260901-DB-EXPLORER-IS-UNGATED-AND-REACHES-DEVICE-TOKENS-RAW-TOKEN-COLUMN` is still open one day after #10682 merged. ⚠️ NEITHER DOES A GREEN TEST: `tests/test_work_decisions.py` already exercises submit→commit→`committed` in a harness (28 passing, and the two load-bearing invariants are mutation-tested). A harness is not the fleet, and the four stages this row lists are precisely the ones a harness cannot reach. ⚠️ NOR DOES A `workflow_dispatch` RUN OF `work-decision-commit` BY ITSELF: it is worth doing FIRST and it clears stage (d) only — a green empty run proves the job can reach the VM and read the log, which is genuinely useful and is NOT the round-trip. Say which stages you cleared rather than clearing the row on the easiest one. ⚠️ AND IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES NOT TO SET `DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN` on the web-api, this row does NOT clear — it CHANGES: answering from the UI is then declared closed, which is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one rather than left looking like a channel that is about to work.
items.probe_absent_reason: A PROBE IS POSSIBLE ONLY AFTER THE DEPLOY, and would be the WRONG OBSERVABLE before it. The machine-readable check is `GET /api/bot/work/decisions` → `summary.byAnswerState.committed >= 1`, which is unreachable while the route 404s on the live host — a probe armed now would sit red on a draft PR, which is the desensitized-alarm P1 this register exists to kill. ⚠️ A probe on `summary.awaitingOperator == 0` would be actively WRONG: zero is the state before anyone writes a question down, and it is indistinguishable from every question having been answered. ⚠️ A probe on the transit log being non-empty would be wrong too — a row there is a SUBMISSION, not a decision, and reading one as the other is exactly what the round-trip's contract refuses.

items.summary: E3 shipped (Phase G): scripts/ops/sunset_pass.py grades retirement candidates weekly, docs/claude/SUNSET-DISPOSITIONS.json records answers, and check_sunset_dispositions.py escalates an unanswered one. Its first run named 10 candidates over 52 legs. ⚠️ NOTHING HAS BEEN RETIRED. The phase's own done-condition — 'something has actually been REMOVED' — is NOT met and was deliberately not claimed: every candidate is either Tier-3 (the operator's call) or a Tier-1 tool where the correct disposition is `wire`/`keep` rather than delete. Shipped and working are different states, and this is the row that keeps them apart.
items.detail: The mechanism is unproven in THREE separate ways and they must not be collapsed. (1) THE CADENCE: the cron fires LATE and ERRATICALLY rather than not at all. CORRECTED 2026-09-02: probes.yml HAS now fired on cron (actions_list on probes.yml, event=schedule, total_count 1, run #34, conclusion success, 2026-09-01T10:12:17Z) and that row is CLEARED. The caution it carried still stands and is now better evidenced, not weaker: its cron is `20 5 * * *` and it fired at 10:12Z, roughly 4h50m LATE, and once rather than daily. So correct cron syntax still is not evidence of a run -- read the run history. So a sunset artifact appearing on a given day is still a real observation and NOT an expectation -- the correction is to the reason, not to the caution. (2) THE ESCALATION: check_sunset_dispositions.py's carry rule needs CARRY_ESCALATION_PASSES=3 accrued passes before it can fire at all, so it is green today by construction and its teeth are asserted only by its self-test. (3) THE DECISION: 10 Tier-3 proposals sit with operator_decision=pending and nobody but their author has read them. ⚠️ The single strongest candidate is `turtle_soup` — enabled: true in config/strategies.yaml, in the strategies list of ZERO accounts, 0 lifetime closed trades. It cannot reach the order path at all. That is either a routing bug or a dead leg, and this row does not presume which.
items.clears_when: A retirement is DONE — the thing is GONE and check_sunset_dispositions.py verified its absence on a `retired` row it did not write itself. ⚠️ A MERGE DOES NOT CLEAR THIS: shipping the pass is a deploy, not an observation, the same distinction that keeps OI-20260826-SESSION-BRIEF-NEVER-READ-BY-A-FRESH-SESSION open. ⚠️ NOR DOES A PASSING SELF-TEST, and this is the specific trap here: both unreachable branches (E2's `enforcing`, E3's carry escalation) are asserted green by their own self-tests today, so a green suite proves the CODE works and says nothing about whether the MECHANISM ever fired. ⚠️ NOR DOES ANOTHER SUNSET PASS RUNNING: more candidates is more detection, and detection was never the missing half — check_unwired_artifacts has reported 115 findings and exited 0 for weeks. The observation wanted is a REMOVAL. ⚠️ AND A DISPOSITION OF `keep` ON EVERYTHING DOES NOT CLEAR IT EITHER: that is a legitimate answer per row and an illegitimate answer for the population, and it would mean the forcing function was answered into inertness — which is a more useful finding than a pass, and belongs in `observation` rather than being treated as a clear.
items.why_it_cannot_be_closed_by_time: Complexity is monotonic by construction until something removes: 6 strategy retirements ever, none in five weeks against 45 live legs, and nothing has ever retired a skill, register, workflow or guard. A retirement mechanism that is never exercised is indistinguishable from the four registers that already report and pass — which is the exact state Phase G was built to end, reproduced one level up inside the fix.

items.summary: The dedicated Claude bot (@ict_cluade_bot) is CONFIGURED and its drain is FIXED and DEPLOYED, and pings still land in the TRADER chat. #10674 is merged (5c45ca52) and live on the VM (1bae542a); the bridge now resolves via claude_route() and at 21:37:08Z logged isolated=False with its own WARNING naming the missing key. What remains is one Tier-2 set-env putting TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET in the VM .env -- which this session could NOT dispatch (issue_write create -> 403) and which needs an operator OK it does not have.
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-01, not inferred. Before the merge, main's router reported isolated=True WHILE the drain sent via TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN -- reproduced by driving the real _drain_pending_claude_pings against both trees with a stubbed telegram module (PR tree 3/3; main fails case 1 with bot_token='trader-tok'). That is why 'the router says isolated' was never evidence: the only consumer that mattered never asked it. AFTER the merge the reading is HONEST -- the live startup line is 'claude ping route -> claude: token=TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN[fallback] chat=TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID[fallback] deliverable=True isolated=False own_chat=False' plus a WARNING. The surface now distinguishes the two states and currently reports the true one. TWO INDEPENDENT BLOCKERS REMAIN, and only one is tooling. (1) set-env is Tier-2 (docs/claude/system-actions.md line 99) and CLAUDE.md requires an operator OK in chat; the instruction to run it came from a MANAGER session, not the operator. (2) NO system-action can be dispatched from a read-only-MCP session at all -- issue_write method=create returns 403, which blocks even Tier-1 send-ping. A push-triggered issue-opener relay would fix (2) and was deliberately NOT built: it needs the PAT (GITHUB_TOKEN-created issues do not trigger workflows, per pr-opener.yml's measured note) and would let any claude/** push fire any allowlisted tiered VM action. Asked on the coordination board instead.
items.clears_when: A ping is CONFIRMED to have arrived in @ict_cluade_bot AND NOT in the trader chat. !! DELIVERY IS NOT THE CRITERION AND MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE. Pings have been delivering throughout -- one enqueued 20:58:49Z on 2026-09-01 was confirmed delivered, to the TRADER chat, while the operator watched the new bot and correctly reported nothing arrived. So 'the ping went out' and 'the drain reported success' clear NOTHING here; the claim is SEPARATION. !! NOR IS THE STARTUP LOG SUFFICIENT ALONE. isolated=True proves which TOKEN the bridge resolved, which is necessary and genuinely new -- but a token is not a conversation, and in a DM the chat_id is the OPERATOR's own id (365546917) for every bot by construction, so the VM side cannot distinguish the two chats even in principle. The last hop is observable only on the operator's phone. Clearing needs BOTH: (a) the startup line reads token=TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET[dedicated] ... isolated=True, AND (b) a human confirms which conversation it appeared in. Either half alone leaves this open.
items.probe_absent_reason: MISSING CAPABILITY, and deliberately NOT a partial probe. The clearing criterion has two halves and only one is machine-observable. The TOKEN half is reachable -- the bridge's startup line is readable via /api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-claude-bridge.service and states token=...[dedicated] ... isolated=True. The CONVERSATION half is not reachable from any surface this repo can query, and not for want of an endpoint: in a Telegram DM the chat.id IS the operator's own user id (365546917) for every bot that messages them, so the VM cannot distinguish 'landed in @ict_cluade_bot' from 'landed in the trader chat' EVEN IN PRINCIPLE. The last hop exists only in the operator's app. A PROBE ON THE OBSERVABLE HALF ALONE WOULD BE WORSE THAN NONE, which is why one is not declared. It would go green the moment the token reaches the .env and would render, on the same surfaces that render every other probe, as this row having been checked and found healthy -- while the thing the row exists to establish had never been looked at. That is the exact substitution this row's clears_when spends its length refusing, and a green probe is a far more persuasive way to make it than a sentence in a summary. IF THE CHANNEL EVER MOVES FROM A DM TO A GROUP OR CHANNEL this reason expires: a per-route TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_CHAT_ID would make the destination a distinct id, targets_own_chat would become meaningful, and getUpdates against the dedicated token would be a real probe. Re-file it then rather than assuming this carries.
items.why_it_cannot_be_closed_by_time: The failure mode is a channel that looks healthy from every surface while landing in the wrong place, which is also what a quiet week looks like. Nothing decays into being fixed: the token is either in the VM .env or it is not, and until someone reads the message in the right app nobody can say which conversation it reached.

items.summary: The M20 E0 live arm now scopes to the round's own legs (`build_exit_head_dataset.py --legs`, passed by `m20_exit_head_round.py` wherever it passes `--db`), fixing defect 1 of BL-20260813-EXIT-HEAD-LIVE-ARM-DROPPED-ON-NO-CANDLES: without it the builder loaded EVERY strategy-attributed closed trade and `family_of()` bucketed same-symbol siblings into families the round never asked for. IT HAS NEVER RUN ON THE TRAINER. The session that shipped it had no `issue_write` (403), so the `trainer-vm-diag-request` relay was unreachable and no round has exercised the flag against a real journal. Shipped and exercised are different states and only the first happened.
items.detail: Verified in a HARNESS, not on the fleet: tests/test_exit_head_live_arm_leg_scoping.py runs six cases against a real sqlite journal, including the positive control that the UNSCOPED load does still pull the same-symbol sibling. What a harness cannot reach here is the SECOND drop stage: the same round's build_report.json showed 701 `no_candles` skips, which this change does not touch, so a real round may STILL return live=0. That is now distinguishable rather than ambiguous -- `legs_filter_state: applied` beside a zero live count says the drop happened at the CANDLE stage and not at leg-selection -- but distinguishable is not measured.
items.clears_when: A REAL ict_scalp exit-head round runs on the trainer and its build_report.json is read, showing BOTH: (a) `legs_filter_state: applied` with `legs_filter` listing exactly the round's `--legs`, and (b) a families dict containing NO family the round did not ask for -- no `donchian`/`pullback` bucket on a scalp round. A NON-ZERO LIVE COUNT IS NOT THE CRITERION and must not be treated as one: the `no_candles` stage is a separate, untouched condition, so a round can be correctly scoped and still read live=0, and reading that as this fix having failed is the exact conflation the three-state `legs_filter_state` exists to prevent. A PASSING UNIT TEST CLEARS NOTHING -- the tests already pass; that is what makes this `awaiting_verification` rather than unproven in principle.

items.summary: The TELEGRAM half of the decision round-trip is built (src/runtime/telegram_decisions.py + a `wdec:*` branch in telegram_query_bot.callback_handler + a job-queue sweep): an unanswered `decision_requests[]` entry is sent to the operator as an inline-keyboard prompt, and a tap POSTs to /api/bot/work/decision over loopback. NOT ONE TAP HAS EVER BEEN MADE. Built, and exercised, are different states and only the first happened. It is also NOT DEPLOYED: the code reaches the VM via ict-git-sync, but `ict-telegram-bot.service` only picks up a new handler and a new job on a RESTART, which is Tier-2 and is the manager's to dispatch.
items.detail: What a harness HAS established (tests/test_telegram_decisions.py, 73 passing): callback_data is 26 bytes fixed against Telegram's 64-byte cap for ids up to 2000 chars; the option token is a digest of the option KEY so reordering the options does not silently select a different answer (a positional index would have); a digest collision is refused rather than resolved by first match; the success reply says `Submitted - NOT yet decided` and the string `committed` does not appear in it; every refusal path states that nothing was submitted, and the one genuinely ambiguous case (no HTTP response at all) says it does NOT know rather than claiming either way; the sweep asks once, only for `not_submitted`, and HOLDS rather than sending buttons that would 503. What a harness CANNOT reach is every stage that matters here: no message has been rendered in Telegram, no button has been tapped, and no submission has travelled the loopback POST. TWO ENVIRONMENT FACTS ARE INFERRED AND NOT MEASURED. (1) DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN is written by scripts/ops/sync_vm_secrets.sh into /home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/.env, which is exactly the EnvironmentFile deploy/ict-telegram-bot.service reads -- so the bot SHOULD hold the bearer, but this session could not read that process's environment (no issue_write, so no `get-env` system-action) and did not verify it. If it is absent the sweep HOLDS and logs a WARNING rather than sending dead buttons; it does not fail open. (2) The destination is the trader bot (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN), chosen because ict-telegram-bot.service is the process that POLLS it. Measured from the repo, not from the VM: ict-claude-bridge.service polls the PROP token despite its name, and TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET -- the dedicated Claude bot -- is polled by NOTHING, so a prompt sent there would render buttons that go nowhere. That is a standing hazard for OI-20260901-CLAUDE-CHANNEL-SEPARATION-SHIPPED-BUT-UNPROVEN: separating the ping channel does not by itself make it answerable, and moving these prompts onto the dedicated bot without also polling it would break them silently.
items.clears_when: The operator's OWN acceptance test completes, end to end, and is RECORDED: (1) a decision request reaches the operator's Telegram as a message with buttons; (2) they tap one; (3) GET /api/bot/work/decisions shows that request as `in_transit` with the transit window open; (4) a LATER read of the same route grades that same request `committed`, with the `answer` block visible in docs/claude/work/objects/<id>.yaml on `main`. [!] STAGES (1)-(3) AND STAGE (4) ARE DIFFERENT FACTS AND MUST BE REPORTED SEPARATELY -- (1)-(3) prove the Telegram half; (4) is the committer, which is OI-20260901-DECISION-ROUNDTRIP-SHIPPED-AND-NO-DECISION-HAS-EVER-MADE-THE-ROUND-TRIP's business and is NOT cleared by this row. Say which stages you actually cleared. [!] A GREEN TEST SUITE CLEARS NOTHING HERE -- the harness already passes and is precisely what cannot reach a rendered message or a real tap. [!] NEITHER DOES MERGING: a merge is not a deploy, and this needs an ict-telegram-bot.service RESTART before the handler or the sweep exists in the running process. [!] AND A QUIET CHANNEL IS NOT EVIDENCE: if no prompt arrives, read /api/diag/log_file?name=work_decision_prompted and the bot's journal before concluding anything -- the sweep HOLDS (with a WARNING naming the reason) when the API's write gate is closed or when no polled bot can carry the buttons, and a hold and an outage are opposite facts that look identical from the operator's phone.

probe.checks: A bybit_coverage_soak row exists in which the SIDE-AWARE grade actually DISAGREED with the side-blind sum (verdicts_differ: true). That is the load-bearing half of this row's threshold: a soak of any length in which the two never diverge shows the gate would change nothing on this book, so a bare row COUNT is not the criterion and the probe deliberately does not test one. The positive control (verdicts_differ present as either true or false) is what separates 'the gate ran and always agreed' from 'the log is absent or unreadable' -- and here that distinction is load-bearing rather than decorative, because 'nothing matched' is the state this row is ALREADY expected to be in, so an unreadable log would emit exactly the answer a reader anticipates. Measured 2026-09-02 the whole file held 28 rows, all with verdicts_differ false, so the control passes today while the requirement does not.
probe.is_not: A PASS DOES NOT CLEAR THIS ROW, and specifically does not satisfy either clause of clears_when. It cannot see the ROW COUNT or the DAY SPAN (>=20 rows over >=3 distinct UTC days), because probe_soak tests for the existence of a matching row and not for a distribution -- so a single disagreement on one day passes this probe and clears nothing. It also cannot make clause (b), which is an OPERATOR DECISION to arm or not to arm; no probe can stand in for that. [!] A FAIL IS NOT EVIDENCE THE GATE IS INERT EITHER: the honest reading of a fail is 'no disagreement has been observed YET', and distinguishing that from 'this gate would never disagree' needs the day span the probe cannot measure. [!] AND IT SAYS NOTHING ABOUT WHETHER THE GATE IS ARMED -- it reads the annotate-mode soak, which is written whether or not BYBIT_GRADED_COVERAGE_ACCOUNTS names an account. Arming is confirmed on /proc/<MainPID>/environ via get-env, never from this log and never from the .env file.

items.summary: #10746 (src/runtime/bybit_coverage_basis.py) is MERGED to main (af9af5e3) and its ARMING IS DELIBERATELY HELD, on an operator instruction given in-conversation 2026-09-02: 'hold it until the soak'. The gate grades a Bybit re-arm against the book actually being protected instead of a side-blind leg sum. It is held at the measurement stage: BYBIT_GRADED_COVERAGE_ACCOUNTS ships EMPTY, and for this knob an empty allowlist means NONE (the PROTECTION_REASSERT_ACCOUNTS polarity, deliberately opposite to CONVICTION_SIZING_ACCOUNTS). [!] THIS ROW EXISTS BECAUSE OF A STANDING OPERATOR RULE, not because the code is suspect: 'anything soaking needs to be logged with an alarm that has either a timer or a soak threshold, so that we know to get back to it when the soak is ready.' Without it the soak accrues and nobody returns, which is how a held decision becomes an abandoned one.
items.detail: WHY THE HOLD IS SATISFIABLE AT ALL, verified by reading the module rather than inferred from the PR title: account_may_apply() returns False for every account when the allowlist is empty or unset, AND the allowlist scopes the BINDING, never the MEASUREMENT: every Bybit account is graded and annotated regardless. So the soak accrues with the arming held, which is exactly the staged posture NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_ACCOUNTS had to be CORRECTED into on 2026-08-09, after intersecting the account set at the top of the pass made the account being staged toward invisible. resolve_mode() falls back to annotate on an unparseable value, never to off and never to apply. [!] MERGED, DEPLOYED and ARMED are three separate facts. The merge is observed (af9af5e3 on main) and the deploy is observed (see observation); ARMED is none of them. [!] DO NOT ARM BY EDITING THE DEFAULT. Arming is a Tier-2 env change on the VM (BYBIT_GRADED_COVERAGE_MODE plus BYBIT_GRADED_COVERAGE_ACCOUNTS) confirmed from /proc/<MainPID>/environ, never from the .env file, which says only what the NEXT restart will pick up. Stage it on bybit_1 (demo); bybit_2 is mainnet.
items.clears_when: THE SOAK THRESHOLD IS STATED SO THIS CANNOT BE CLEARED BY IMPATIENCE OR RUN FOREVER. Clears when BOTH: (a) the soak log holds at least 20 graded rows spanning at least 3 distinct UTC days on at least one Bybit account, AND at least one row where the side-aware grade DIFFERS from the side-blind sum (verdicts_differ true); and (b) the operator, shown that row count and at least one concrete disagreement, decides to arm or not to arm. [!] A COUNT OF ROWS IS NOT THE CRITERION ON ITS OWN: 20 rows in which every grade agrees means the gate is inert on this book, and arming it would be a change with no measured effect. Record that and say so rather than arming to close the row. [!] DECIDING NOT TO ARM CLEARS THIS ROW TOO, and must be RECORDED as a decision rather than left looking like a soak still running: that is the failure mode the rule exists to catch. [!] AN EMPTY SOAK DOES NOT CLEAR IT AND IS ITSELF THE FINDING: zero rows after 3 days means the code is not deployed or not reached, which is a deploy defect, not a quiet book. Zero rows and twenty-agreeing rows are opposite facts and must never both be reported as 'the soak is quiet'.
items.observation: 2026-09-09, MI-225 audit: THE SOAK IS ACCRUING AND ITS OWN CLEARS_WHEN IS UNSATISFIABLE BY CONSTRUCTION - a new fact about this row, not a restatement. It requires 'at least 20 graded rows spanning at least 3 distinct UTC days'. MEASURED: /api/diag/log_file?name=bybit_coverage_soak returns the 1000-line cap spanning 7.24 HOURS at 2.30 rows/min, which is 2.5% of the file - so 3 distinct UTC days needs roughly 17x the hard read ceiling. _MAX_LIMIT is 1000 and _clamp SILENTLY reduces anything larger, so this is the ceiling for every consumer, not a parameter choice. The rows ACCRUE fine; they cannot be READ BACK. An evidence store unreadable past ~7 hours is weak evidence for a real-money arming decision, and this row's evidence is the declared basis for widening the gate to bybit_2. NOT CLEARED, and the operator should know the criterion cannot be met before being asked to act on it. Proposed fix: offset/since paging on /api/diag/log_file, with a positive control that an out-of-range window returns an explicit empty state rather than silently serving the tail. Same ceiling behind 17 of 54 truncated soaks measured this pass.

items.summary: Work-decision prompts are re-pointed from the TRADER bot to the dedicated Claude bot (@ict_cluade_bot), and the thing that makes that safe ships in the SAME PR: src/bot/claude_decision_bot.py + deploy/ict-claude-decision-bot.service POLL TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET and register the same `wdec` handler, so the bot is ANSWERABLE before anything is routed to it. Operator, 2026-09-02: "that's supposed to be showing up in Cloudbot. Right? Not on the trader one, the decisions." !! NO TAP HAS EVER BEEN MADE ON CLAUDEBOT. The PR is a DRAFT, the new unit has never run, and whether TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET is present in the VM .env is NOT something this session could read -- that is an operator/manager action, not a bug to work around, and it must not be substituted with TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_TOKEN (which drives the PROP bot despite its name).
items.detail: WHAT A HARNESS HAS ESTABLISHED (111 passing: the 73 pre-existing tests/test_telegram_decisions.py plus 38 new): answerable_route() prefers the Claude bot ONLY on positive poll evidence; `unknown` (we could not look) fails closed and is never collapsed into `token_only_not_polled` (we looked and a tap would not be received); the sweep HOLDS with a WARNING naming a state-specific REMEDY when no bot is confirmed polled, counted as `held_not_polled` and never pooled with `held_route` (no destination at all); a heartbeat expires a dead process's claim; no token VALUE reaches a note, banner or persisted entry; and the /api/diag/log_file paths match what the writer actually produces. !! WHAT A HARNESS CANNOT REACH IS THE ENTIRE POINT OF THIS ROW. Every one of those facts is equally true of a process that is never started. The failure this change exists to prevent -- a prompt that ARRIVES, RENDERS and HIGHLIGHTS ON TAP while nothing collects the callback_query -- has no external symptom, so green CI is precisely the evidence that cannot settle it. !! AND THE FALLBACK MAKES THE FAILURE QUIET-BUT-WORKING, WHICH IS ITS OWN READING HAZARD: with the Claude bot unconfirmed the sweep routes to the TRADER bot, so 'decisions still arrive' is NOT evidence the move happened. Read `destination` in the sweep stats, or /api/diag/log_file?name=telegram_poll_claude -- never the mere arrival of a prompt. NOT VERIFIED BY ME, and inherited rather than measured: I am told the round trip is already proven on the TRADER bot as of 2026-09-02T10:16:36Z (chosen: accept_ungated, submitted_by: telegram). runtime_logs/ is gitignored, so the transit log is unreachable from a session clone and I did not confirm it. This change moves WHERE the round trip happens, not whether it works.
items.clears_when: A REAL TAP ON CLAUDEBOT PRODUCES A work_decision_transit.jsonl ROW, and it is recorded which request and who tapped. Concretely, all four: (1) ict-claude-decision-bot.service is enabled and ACTIVE on the VM (/api/diag/services), with its startup banner in `journalctl -u ict-claude-decision-bot` naming token_var=TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET and the wdec prefix; (2) /api/diag/log_file?name=telegram_poll_claude returns a FRESH heartbeat; (3) a decision prompt is observed arriving in @ict_cluade_bot and NOT in the trader chat -- the last hop is visible only on the operator's phone, the same limit that keeps OI-20260901-CLAUDE-CHANNEL-SEPARATION-SHIPPED-BUT-UNPROVEN open; (4) the operator taps a button and a row lands in /api/diag/log_file?name=work_decision_transit. !! MERGING DOES NOT CLEAR THIS -- a merge is not a deploy and a deploy is not a tap; the unit must be installed and enabled, which install_systemd_units.sh does only on the next deploy run. !! A GREEN TEST RUN DOES NOT CLEAR THIS, for the reason in `detail`. !! CLAUSE (1) OR (2) ALONE DOES NOT CLEAR IT EITHER: those prove the bot is POLLED, which is necessary and is NOT the same as a tap being RECEIVED and SUBMITTED -- that exact distinction is the subject of this change, and clearing on the cheaper half would reproduce it. !! IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES NOT TO PUT TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET ON THE VM, this row does not clear -- it CHANGES: the trader-bot fallback is then the DECLARED destination, which is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one rather than left looking like a move that is about to happen.

A cron that advanced the readout alone would leave CLAUDE.md quoting the PREVIOUS headline under a NEW file's date -- i.e. it would RELOCATE this staleness into the one surface that reaches a session before it acts, which is strictly worse than the bug it replaces. The two are committed together, always. !! A STALENESS GUARD WAS DELIBERATELY NOT USED INSTEAD. A `--check` on freshness would red every open PR whenever the world moved, which is BL-20260830-A-TRANSIENT-RED-BASE-PERMANENTLY-STRANDS-AN-AUTOMERGE-BRANCH and is why session-brief-guard had to be diff-scoped against origin/main. items.observation: CORRECTED AND ROOT-CAUSED 2026-09-08 by MI-196 (session_01U2ibSa4FNcuV6bSLaPb9GS), superseding the 2026-09-06 re-affirmation -- WHOSE ARITHMETIC WAS SOUND AND WHOSE CONCLUSION WAS WRONG, which is the part worth carrying. That session could not read the run history (api.github.com 403 at its container proxy, no actions_list in its tool surface) and reasoned from CONSTRAINT.json's population not advancing 587 -> 628 that the cron had NOT FIRED. It had fired, six times, and produced no commit because it FAILED. The arithmetic cannot separate `did not fire` from `fired and failed`, and it read as the first. The run-history read was the missing half, not a redundant one. ROOT CAUSE, established and reproduced rather than inferred. The workflow runs actions/setup-python@v5 and installed NOTHING, so PyYAML was absent on the runner. scripts/ops/constraint_readout.py guards its own import (`except ImportError: yaml = None`) and survives; scripts/ci/check_wip_ceiling.py imports yaml at MODULE scope, so `from check_wip_ceiling import CEILING as WIP_CEILING` (constraint_readout.py:107) raised, the broad `except Exception` set WIP_CEILING = None, and the self-test printed `FAIL - the WIP ceiling is imported from the enforcing guard (got None, want 8)` / `1 FAILURE(S)` / exit 1. REPRODUCED LOCALLY with a meta_path finder making `import yaml` raise: the identical single failure. POSITIVE CONTROL: yaml present -> ALL PASS. THE GATE WAS NOT THE DEFECT -- without yaml the work store is unreadable, so a run that skipped the self-test would have committed a readout diagnosing nothing straight into the session brief. Do not `fix` a future failure here by loosening it. FIXED IN PR #11384 by adding a PyYAML install step; nothing else in the workflow's logic, gating, permissions or schedule was touched. THAT IS A DEPLOY, NOT A RUN, and this row stays OPEN on its own clears_when. SECOND, SEPARATE FACT the fix does not touch: against the declared `5 6 * * *` the six runs started 10:28Z, 10:47Z, 11:05Z, 11:07Z, 11:07Z and 12:18Z -- 4.4 to 6.2 hours LATE, every time. Record how late the qualifying run fires when this clears. [!] AND THIS ROW NOW BLOCKS AN OPERATOR DECISION. MI-196 ported the due-list's source classes into the readout as section 5 (#11369, #11378, merged and verified rendering every row on main) under the operator decision `consolidate_into_the_readout`, whose second half retires docs/claude/DUE.md. THE RETIREMENT IS HELD HERE. Carriers, populations stated: due-list.yml has 8 scheduled runs (2026-09-01..09-08) of which 6 succeeded, 1 cancelled, 1 failed; constraint-readout.yml has 6 of which 0 succeeded. Retiring DUE.md before this clears would move the only session-facing due list from a carrier that mostly fires onto one that has never once succeeded -- the same takes-the-due-list-to-zero hazard the operator's two-change condition exists to prevent, arriving through a dead carrier rather than an incomplete port. Backlog: BL-20260908-CONSTRAINT-READOUT-CRON-HAS-FAILED-6-OF-6-SCHEDULED-RUNS-ON-A-MISSING-PYYAML. [!] A SECOND OPEN-ITEMS ROW FOR THE FIX WAS DRAFTED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FILED: it waited on the SAME observation this row waits on, and two rows on one observation is the duplication the register exists to prevent. items.summary: The operating model's anti-silo mechanism is `context = work object + role pack`, and its two halves were wired to different systems: the object half shipped 2026-09-01 and not one role pack knew it existed. Six situating packs (session-coordination, session-handoff, doc-freshness, duty, research-driver, delegate-work) now name the work store, the cycle priority, the constraint readout and the enforced WIP ceiling -- and scripts/ci/check_role_pack_operating_layer.py KEEPS them pointing there, because a one-time prose edit decays silently on the next rewrite. !! NO SESSION HAS BEEN OBSERVED ACTING ON ANY OF IT.
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-02 on the PRE-EDIT tree, and it CORRECTS the audit in one place: docs/audits/operating-layer-skills-workflows-inventory-2026-09-02.md reports `docs/claude/work` at 0 skills; it was 2 (delegate-work, workplan-vs-architecture, both via SESSIONS.json). That sharpens the finding rather than weakening it -- every remaining term was genuinely 0: `work object`, `WIP`, `blocked_on`, `CYCLE-PRIORITY`, `READOUT`, `SUNSET-DISPOSITIONS`, `MANAGER-LEASE`. Only the sub-session REGISTRY was ever wired; the entire STEERING half was invisible. !! THE GUARD PROVES POINTING, NOT READING. It checks two directions -- a situating pack must NAME a live layer path, and every layer path ANY pack names must EXIST, so renaming the store reddens the packs pointing at the old place. Neither direction can observe a session reading one, which is the thing this row is actually for. !! DELIBERATELY NOT ALL 32 PACKS: most are domain procedure and are correctly indifferent to where work is tracked; a blanket requirement would be the 'carrying everything' failure the model warns against.

A GREEN GUARD DOES NOT CLEAR THIS -- it proves the pointer exists, which is a deploy, not a reading; the same distinction that keeps OI-20260826-SESSION-BRIEF-NEVER-READ-BY-A-FRESH-SESSION open. !! A SESSION POINTED HERE BY ITS PROMPT CANNOT CLEAR IT, for the reason the MHG row names: it has been told. !! AND 'a session read it and ignored it' does NOT clear this either -- that is a different and more useful finding, and belongs in `observation` rather than being treated as a pass.

items.summary: replay-pregate-nightly's nightly red is NOT a network fault and NOT an OOM kill -- the trainer VM is out of memory and swap-thrashing, and the fleet run cannot finish. MEASURED on run #4390 (workflow_dispatch, 2026-09-02, the first run with the detach+poll repair): `free -m` on the trainer read total 5909 / used 5508 / free 70 / available 204 MB, with 4095 MB of 8191 MB swap consumed. Both OOM greps -- `dmesg -T` and `journalctl --since -2h` -- returned EMPTY, so nothing was killed; the driver is alive and crawling. It scored 10 of 22 heads in 30 minutes and was still going.
items.detail: WHY THIS COULD NOT BE SEEN BEFORE, and why the repair was worth doing even though it does not fix the cause. Every previous run died at ~8m55s with `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe` at head 10/22 -- 7 of the 8 most recent scheduled runs, with two read in full (#4330, #4335->#4365) and IDENTICAL. A thrashing box stops answering its sshd, so the single long-lived interactive channel dropped and the job reported `no JSON object in driver output`: a parse error standing in for a memory problem, which is why five sessions in a row could act on none of it. With the run DETACHED the transport stopped being the confound: #4390's poll survived its entire 30-minute budget with ZERO transport failures, salvaged 10 heads, and the failure-path evidence step returned the numbers above. [!] SO THE TRANSPORT REPAIR IS PROVEN AND THE WORKFLOW IS STILL RED, and those are different facts. [!] THE OOM HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED, NOT UNCONFIRMED -- the shipping session deliberately declined to assert it, and the kernel evidence says it would have been wrong. [!] A THIRD DEFECT WAS FOUND BY THE SAME RUN AND IS PRE-EXISTING: the commit-back step ran `git add "$DIR"` on runtime_logs/replay_pregate, which .gitignore:29 refuses outright, so under `set -e` it destroyed the 10 salvaged heads. `git ls-tree -r origin/main -- runtime_logs/replay_pregate/` returns ZERO files across the repo's whole fetched history while 72 other runtime_logs files ARE tracked -- so this workflow's own header claim, that it 'commits the report back to the repo, so the result survives a dead Claude session', has been false since it was written, on the COMPLETE path as much as the partial one. Fixed with `git add -f`.
items.clears_when: EITHER (a) a run of replay-pregate-nightly completes all 22 heads and its report lands under runtime_logs/replay_pregate/ ON MAIN -- both halves, because the commit-back has never once worked and a green run that commits nothing would leave the header's claim still false; OR (b) the operator decides the trainer's memory is not going to be increased and the fleet run is re-scoped to fit it (fewer heads per run, or batched across runs), and that decision is RECORDED as a decision rather than left looking like a repair that is about to happen. [!] A PARTIAL RUN DOES NOT CLEAR THIS however many heads it salvages -- salvage is the failure being survived, not the failure being fixed. [!] NEITHER DOES THE TRANSPORT REPAIR, which is already proven and is a DIFFERENT fact: #4390 held the connection for 30 minutes with zero transport failures and the workflow was still red. [!] AND DO NOT CLEAR THIS ON A QUIET ALARM. The workflow is in claude-run-failure-alert.yml's watch list, so it pages nightly; the pages going quiet would mean it stopped RUNNING, not that it started passing. Read the run history.

items.summary: MI-70 built the missing Phase E reaper (scripts/ops/session_reaper.py + .github/workflows/session-reaper.yml) and RAN THE KILL. !! THE HEADLINE IS THAT WO-20260901-PHASE-E'S DONE-CONDITION AS WRITTEN IS FALSE, and the measurement says so rather than being shaped to pass. A purpose-made expendable subject (session_01NN97cVYW5dmiNNXHfsu7Nn) was archived at 2026-09-02T13:49:13Z while SESSION_STATUS_RUNNING, holding three tiers of state. SURVIVED: the pushed tier, entirely -- branch claude/mi70-kill-subject @ 4d9c0c48, content intact. LOST: the committed-but-unpushed commit (its own final status_detail confirms it existed -- 'local phase 2 commit held') and the uncommitted file. So the demonstrated statement is 'killing a session loses everything it had not pushed, and nothing it had', NOT 'loses nothing'. Neither loss is recoverable by any reaper, ever; it lived in a released container. !! THE RECOVERY DID NOT COME FROM SESSIONS.json -- the subject was deliberately never registered, so the registry contributed nothing. The reaper located it by the `Claude-Session:` commit trailer 62s after the kill. What it could NOT recover is what the work was FOR: `owns_object` exists only in the registry.
items.clears_when: THREE PARTS, and they are different facts. (1) The reaper's SCHEDULE is OBSERVED firing -- a `session-reaper` run with event=schedule in actions_list, AND a REAPER-OBSERVATIONS.json whose `generated_at` advanced because of it. !! MERGING IS NOT THIS. This repo has scheduled workflows that are merged, enabled, correct and fire LATE AND ERRATICALLY: probes.yml's first-ever scheduled run came ~4h50m late against `20 5 * * *`, once rather than daily. Correct cron syntax is not evidence of a run -- read the run history. (2) A session OTHER than MI-70 reads the ledger and ACTS on a row in it. A producer with no consumer is the exact shape provenance-consumer-guard exists to catch, and is how the `Claude-Session:` trailer sat unread in the first place. Record WHICH session and WHICH row. (3) The operator or the manager rules on whether Phase E's done-condition is AMENDED to the demonstrated truth, or whether the unpushed tiers are to be closed some other way. !! DO NOT CLOSE PHASE E ON THIS DEMONSTRATION ALONE: it shows a PARTIAL loss, and closing an object on evidence that contradicts its own done-condition is worse than leaving it open. !! AND A CLEAN REAPER REPORT DOES NOT CLEAR THIS: the reaper is blind to unpushed work by construction and cannot tell alive from dead, so its silence is never evidence that nothing was lost.

items.summary: The decision push-back's REPO half is built and its DELIVERY half has never run once. asked_by records which session asked (measured before: of 584 objects, ZERO requests named their asker, so every committed answer had NO ADDRESS); push_decisions_back.py exposes the queue with the message pre-rendered, writes the repo-sourced idempotence marker, and records a per-run receipt; check_drain_liveness.py grades that receipt. [!] THE DRAIN ROUTINE DOES NOT EXIST. [!] THIS ROW SAID 'Nothing in the repo can create it -- a Routine is made from the web UI or /schedule in an interactive CLI session'. THAT PREMISE IS FALSE AND WAS DISPROVEN 2026-09-05T10:39Z, incidentally, while building the manager wake: `create_trigger` through the Claude Code Remote MCP SUCCEEDS from an ordinary session (trig_018AkCBVYcWGCXujNQVrZ92h, cron `39 * * * *`, create_new_session_on_fire=true, verified by firing it). What IS refused is the `connectors` parameter, org-wide and verbatim. So a session CAN create this drain Routine; what it cannot do is give the fired session tools. [!] CREATING IT TODAY WOULD THEREFORE BE HARMFUL, not progress: a fired session gets no mcp__* tools, so it could not poke anything, and it would ALSO block on a permission prompt with no human to answer -- both measured on the wake fire, which landed nothing at all. A drain that exists and delivers nothing is precisely the looks-armed-is-not failure this row already warns about, one level up. [!] THE CORRECTION MATTERS BECAUSE THE REASON CHANGED, NOT THE VERDICT: the blocker is not 'no session can create a Routine', it is 'a Routine-fired session has no tools and cannot answer a prompt'. A session reading the old sentence would conclude the wrong thing about what is possible and would not look at the real obstacle. See BL-20260905-THE-MANAGER-WAKE-ROUTINE-IS-CREATABLE-BUT-CAN-NEITHER-POKE-NOR-LAND-A-RECEIPT -- so the probe grades `never_ran` today and that is CORRECT, not a bug. [!] THE OPERATOR RULED OUT THE CREDENTIAL PATH (2026-09-02): no minted tokens, ever. The claude -p --cloud steps were DELETED rather than left behind an unset secret, because a step wired to a credential nobody will mint is the looks-armed-is-not failure this row exists to watch for.
items.detail: MECHANISMS, proven vs not: A (session-bound Routine wake) is PROVEN -- measured by the manager 2026-09-02T05:35Z and again by the fact that the operator decision behind this row arrived in the session that way (trig_01RPhHB9tEQ87DeaYQ3oQWc2) -- but it CANNOT be the floor, because the caller must be a live session holding mcp__* tools. B (hourly cron Routine, fresh session per fire) is the floor and is UNPROVEN. C (never push into a live session; a blocking question ends its session and a fresh one resumes from the work object) is the DESIGN and is UNPROVEN -- it rests on WO-20260901-PHASE-E, whose exit condition is 'killing a session mid-work loses nothing, DEMONSTRATED by killing one', and NOBODY HAS KILLED ONE. resume_context is the substrate only. [!] A CORRECTION THIS ROW CARRIES SO IT IS NOT RE-DERIVED: the dispatch named `next_run_at: 0001-01-01` as the inert-Routine signature. MEASURED over this account's 10 listed Routines, 7 carry it and they are the manager's OWN poke-only session-bound Routines -- mechanism A, working. The routines docs say a Routine with no schedule trigger has no next run time and older clients rendered it as year 1, so that value means 'no schedule attached' and a watcher keyed on it would flag the working pokes as dead. `last_run` is absent on all ten (list_triggers records no run for a Routine that wakes its own bound session). AND list_triggers is an mcp__* tool, so no runner or CI job can read any of it -- which is why the watcher grades a COMMITTED RECEIPT instead. Full design: docs/design/decision-push-back-DESIGN.md.
items.clears_when: ONE committed answer is OBSERVED reaching the session that asked it, end to end: (1) a decision request carries an `asked_by` block naming a real session; (2) it is answered and the answer COMMITS to main; (3) the drain Routine fires and records `pushed` for it; and (4) THE ASKING SESSION IS OBSERVED WAKING -- idle/disconnected before and running/connected after via get_session, doing something ATTRIBUTABLE to the pushed answer. Record which request and which session. [!] STAGE (4) IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. `pushed` means the drain reported firing, which is a claim about the CALL, not an observation of a wake. [!] A GREEN PROBE CLEARS NOTHING. check_drain_liveness.py grading `fresh` says the drain RAN; it says nothing about whether a delivery succeeded or whether the woken session acted. That is stated in the probe's own is_not for exactly this reason. [!] `never_ran` IS NOT A FAILURE OF THIS ROW TODAY -- it is the accurate reading until the Routine is created, and the row should not be re-filed as broken on the strength of it. [!] AND IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES NOT TO CREATE THE DRAIN ROUTINE, THIS ROW DOES NOT CLEAR -- IT CHANGES: push-back is then carried by mechanism A alone (a manager poking while alive), which is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one, with the consequence stated -- there is then no floor, and a committed answer whose asker is idle when no manager is alive is never delivered.

probe.checks: Whether the decision push-back drain has recorded a run inside its window, graded over the committed receipt docs/claude/work/DECISION-DRAIN.json. Four states, never collapsed: fresh / stale (ran before, has stopped) / never_ran (created and never fired -- a DIFFERENT fix) / unreadable (we could not look; never a pass). probe.is_not: A PASS says the DRAIN RAN. It does NOT say a delivery succeeded, does NOT say the asking session woke, and does NOT say the woken session acted -- those are stage (3) and (4) of clears_when and no probe can reach them. A FAIL of `never_ran` is currently the CORRECT reading (the Routine has not been created yet) and is not evidence of a regression. The probe also cannot see a Routine that exists but was created WITHOUT a schedule trigger: that is indistinguishable from no Routine at all, and shows up only as never_ran.

If no session has needed an endpoint contract in a week the question has simply not been asked; if sessions HAVE needed one and quietly worked around the pointer, that is the failure and it is invisible from the calendar. probe.checks: Grades the AGE of docs/claude/work/PR-QUEUE-WATCH.json, the receipt pr-queue-watch.yml writes on every run. Four states, never collapsed: `fresh` (a run inside the 30h window) / `stale` (the watcher HAS run and has STOPPED — the failure this exists for) / `never_ran` (no receipt at all — a DIFFERENT fact needing a different fix: create/repair the cadence, not investigate a regression) / `unreadable` (WE COULD NOT LOOK — a corrupt receipt, which is not evidence about the watcher and fails loudly rather than passing quietly).
probe.is_not: ⚠️ A PASS DOES NOT CLEAR THIS ROW, and today a pass is the EXPECTED result while the cron has never fired: `never_ran` deliberately EXITS 0, because failing would red every PR in the repo on merge day — how a guard gets disabled instead of fixed. So this probe cannot distinguish 'the watcher is healthy' from 'the watcher has never existed' by exit code alone; READ THE STATE IT PRINTS. ⚠️ It also says nothing about whether the SCHEDULE works: a workflow_dispatch run writes an identical receipt, and the failure class being watched is a cron that never fires (probes.yml's first scheduled run was ~4h50m late and fired once instead of daily). Clause (1) of clears_when therefore requires a SCHEDULED run observed in the run history, which no probe can read from here. ⚠️ And it grades the WATCHER, never the QUEUE: a large backlog of unmerged PRs passes this probe by design.

items.summary: ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-09-04 — THE HEADLINE IN THIS ROW'S OWN ID IS NOW FALSE AND THE ID IS KEPT ONLY BECAUSE OTHER ROWS LINK IT BY NAME: THE CRON HAS FIRED. This one lands its receipt through .github/actions/commit-to-main with verify-merged, so an unmerged receipt fails the run rather than exiting 0 on a PR that merely exists. verified_at is deliberately null: no observation has been made, and dating it today would be a claim of one.
items.detail: WHAT WAS MEASURED, AND OVER WHAT POPULATION. 2026-09-02T17:21Z, population = ALL 10 open, unmerged PRs on this repo; quiescence = hours since the last commit on the head branch. The distribution is cleanly BIMODAL: 0.2 / 1.0 / 1.0 h, then a gap, then 5.3 / 5.7 / 7.4 / 7.7 / 11.0 / 18.9 / 109.5 h. The nearest observations either side of the gap are 1.0h and 5.3h, so every threshold in (1.0, 5.3] separates 'being worked' from 'handed back' identically on this data; 6h was chosen just past it, and independently equals four manager-lease TTLs (90 min) — a PR that has outlived every manager that could have merged it. ⚠️ n = 10 IS A SMALL DENOMINATOR and one repo on one day is not a distribution; the value is defensible, not calibrated. THE PROXY IS A PROXY AND IS LABELLED AS ONE. Branch quiescence indicates HAND-BACK; it is not proof of one, because a session can be alive with nothing pushed. So the watcher never claims a session is dead and never merges, closes, un-drafts or comments — the same reason session_reaper.py is permitted to grade the same proxy ('the cost of calling a live session stalled_with_work is a refreshed row in a ledger'). VALIDATED AGAINST THE KNOWN FAILURE: the live run flagged #10694, whose MANAGER-CHECKLIST row (MI-18) records its owner as 'session_01LqVvgvusnN87neBn5ayzhg (archived; its PR #10694 stands)' while the item state reads `in_flight`. The watcher caught exactly the case the manager's own record mislabels. THREE OF THE FOUR HYPOTHESISED PROXIES DO NOT WORK, MEASURED. (B) 'a PR whose owner posted needs_action' — needs_action lives ONLY in SESSIONS.json's last_observed, a SNAPSHOT the sweep prompt already warns must not be read as current, carried by 4 of 74 rows, and written to no GitHub surface at all; a staleness detector running on stale data reports a healthy queue with total confidence. (C) 'a board START with no DONE' — every comment on #6927 is authored by the repo OWNER regardless of which session wrote it, so pairing is free-text parsing, and the sessions most needing to be caught are precisely the ones that died before posting anything; it would fire permanently, which is the desensitised-alarm P1. (D) 'a checklist item in_flight whose owner's branch is quiet' — UNCOMPUTABLE: measured over MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json, 0 of 23 `in_flight` items carry a branch and 0 carry a PR number (across all 72 items: 0 branches, 2 PR entries). The join does not exist. WHAT THE GUARD DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: it grades the watcher's LIVENESS and never the backlog's SIZE. run_guards.py already records why a live open-PR read does not belong in per-PR CI ('reddening PRs for a row nobody could have written yet'), and a contributor going red because the manager has four other PRs unmerged would train everyone past the guard. Escalation instead rides a deliberate failure of the watcher's own run, picked up by claude-run-failure-alert.yml, latched by band + cooldown, addressed to the OPERATOR rather than the manager who is the bottleneck being reported on.

items.detail: THIS IS A RECURRENCE, and that is the finding more than the missing pings. BL-20260830-SCHEDULED-WORKFLOW-LAG-WENT-FROM-1H-TO-6-12H-ON-2026-08-27 is OPEN and already said 'ANY plan whose correctness depends on a cron firing at roughly its declared time is now wrong'. Three days later the operator's ping cadence -- which F6 makes the CONDITION the autonomy grant rests on -- was put on exactly that carrier and nobody read the row. The earlier fix did not hold because it was a row nobody read, not a mechanism. MEASURED CARRIER EVIDENCE for the unfixed half: of 26 LIVE Routines (list_triggers limit=100, next_cursor None; include_completed defaults false so fired one-shots are hidden), 25 are bound to one persistent_session_id and die with it. The ONE that is not, trig_01TWdAvrwFLe6T9XFoNopTeo, is also the only one carrying an observable last_run: it fired 42s after its :56 slot into a NEW session. So a fresh-session Routine is both reliable and creator-independent, measured rather than assumed. A ~4x/day WATCHDOG Routine (not the digest itself, which would cost 24 sessions/day) is the proposal; creating it is recurring spend on the operator's account and was deliberately NOT done. A VM systemd timer was assessed and cannot carry the digest -- VM_GIT_DEPLOY_TOKEN is Contents:read-only so the VM cannot push to main -- but is a real Tier-2 candidate for the watchdog.

This row's own words — 'a push-driven digest cannot produce a heartbeat while main is quiet' — are now MEASURED, not merely argued. ⚠️ SECOND-ORDER COST THIS ROW DID NOT ANTICIPATE: the guard runs in `guards` on every PR, so a stale digest REDS EVERY OPEN PR, and its remedy is a push to main that a PR cannot make while it is red. probe.checks: A work-digest job log contains the literal `work-digest: trigger=push`, i.e. a run of that workflow was carried by a PUSH event. That is the only thing that settles clause (1): the workflow file declaring `push` is a declaration, and this repo's whole finding is that a declared trigger is not a run. The positive control is `work-digest: trigger=` WITHOUT the event value, so a log that is fetched but no longer carries the line at all grades could_not_run rather than a clean negative -- the unstated-denominator error one level up.
probe.is_not: A PASS DOES NOT CLEAR THIS ROW. It establishes that a push-triggered run EXISTED; it says nothing about (a) whether that run actually queued a digest -- the gate may have graded `not_due` and skipped, which is correct behaviour and not a delivery, (b) whether the receipt docs/claude/work/WORK-DIGEST.json LANDED on main, which is the fact clause (1) actually requires and which only a read of main can show, (c) clause (2) at all, the detector arming itself on a PR other than #10845, and (d) the QUIET-WINDOW half, which is the part this change does not fix -- a push-triggered run is by definition evidence from a period when main was NOT quiet, so it is the wrong population for that question entirely. A FAIL today is the CORRECT reading, not a defect: nothing has fired yet.

items.detail: ⚠️ A CLOUD ROUTINE IS REFUSED AND MUST NOT BE PROPOSED IN ANY FORM, including a fresh-session-per-fire variant — operator, 2026-09-02, verbatim: 'no cloud routine. We can't have anything that's gonna die at the end of the session… You cannot create a Band Aid that's gonna get lost as soon as the session is over.' One was created earlier that day and has been deleted. ⚠️ A TRAP FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT, and the reason the carrier is a NEW runner rather than a call to the existing one: `work_digest.py --write` latches DAY-granular on runtime_logs/work_digest_state.json. That latch is INERT in CI — runtime_logs/ is gitignored, so a fresh runner never has the file, which is why 3 digests landed on 2026-09-02 despite it — and it would be LIVE on the VM, silently capping an hourly carrier at ONE digest per day with no error and no sign anything was suppressed. scripts/ops/work_digest_now.py keeps its own HOUR-granular latch in its own receipt and never reads or writes the workflow's, asserted BEHAVIOURALLY (plant a day latch, require a send) rather than by a source grep. It also reads the standing close-wedge ledger LOCALLY rather than over diag, so no token and no diag outage can degrade that section.

items.summary: #10944 MERGED (squash 717f00eb, Tier-2, operator-approved 2026-09-03) makes the trader's monitor sweep heartbeat an empty-but-PRESENT close-wedge ledger, and stops the reader synthesising a clean fleet from `present: false`. ⚠️ THE LEDGER HAS NEVER BEEN OBSERVED PRESENT ON THE FLEET. items.detail: WHAT IT REPLACED, measured before the merge: all 12 work-digest rows in docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl read `Standing close wedges: none (ledger read, 0 entries) — a real observation, not an absence of one.` Every word of that was false. The trader had NEVER written the ledger (`sweep_vanished` returned before touching disk whenever no wedge was carried, which is the overwhelmingly common case), diag answered `present: false`, and `fetch_standing_wedges` converted that into a SYNTHESISED empty ledger — the `curl … || echo '{}'` idiom, in Python, inside the function written to prevent it, shipped with a self-test asserting the defect as correct. ⚠️ EXPECT A VISIBLE AND CORRECT REGRESSION IN THE OPERATOR CHANNEL FIRST: until the trader restarts with the heartbeat the digest reports NOT EXAMINED instead of the false clean bill. That is the honest state of a ledger nothing writes, it is strictly more informative, and it self-resolves on the next deploy — DO NOT roll it back and do not file it as a regression. ⚠️ ONE INCIDENTAL OBSERVATION THE PR FLAGGED AND DID NOT ACT ON, still owed to somebody: CLAUDE.md records Alpaca GLD OCO parent 2e843e04 as `pending_cancel` since 2026-08-27, and /api/diag/alpaca_open_orders read it as `new` on 2026-09-03 while the position is open and the close is still failing (155 consecutive). The wedge's CLASSIFICATION has moved away from what that row expects. PAPER, not real money.

items.detail:
WHY THERE IS NO ROUTINE, measured in both directions rather than assumed. (a) `create_trigger` through the Claude Code Remote MCP returns `mcp_connections: []` and warns that the sessions it fires run WITHOUT `mcp__*` tools — and the wake's poke step IS `create_trigger` + `fire_trigger`, so such a Routine could assess and record and NEVER WAKE ANYONE. (b) Passing the `connectors` parameter is refused outright: 'the connectors parameter is not available for this organization.' (c) Sub-hourly is also refused: `*/30 * * * *` -> 'the minimum interval is 1 hour', which is the MEASURED basis for the ~30-90 minute bound this work claims rather than an assumption.

An hourly Routine WAS created (trig_014XUfC9M5aL5FsJwHhkhQkY), confirmed inert, and DELETED rather than left in place — the operator's own standard, recorded in OI-20260902-DECISION-DRAIN-ROUTINE-DOES-NOT-EXIST-AND-NOTHING-HAS-EVER-DRAINED, where the `claude -p --cloud` steps were deleted rather than left behind an unset secret 'precisely so nothing looks armed and is not'. A Routine named `manager-wake` that cannot wake is that failure wearing the fix's name.

WHAT THE OPERATOR MUST DO: create it from claude.ai/code/routines with the Claude Code Remote connector attached, pasting the committed prompt at docs/claude/work/manager-wake-routine-prompt.md. This is the SAME constraint decision-drain-routine-prompt.md already records for the drain — two mechanisms now blocked on one operator action, which is itself worth noticing.

⚠️ THE REAPER IS A DIFFERENT ROW, NOT THIS ONE. The wake covers an ALIVE-AND-SILENT manager; a manager that DIED cannot be poked at all, and `assess` reports that as `no_manager` and deliberately does nothing. Filed as BL-20260904-NOTHING-REAPS-A-DEAD-MANAGER-OR-CLAIMS-AN-EXPIRED-LEASE.

items.summary: MI-128 / PR #11037 re-keys `_sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced`'s scan window and ORDER BY from `created_at` (the OPEN) to `COALESCE(closed_at, created_at)` (the CLOSE). Keyed on the open, a position held longer than 14 days was already outside the window when it closed and stayed outside forever — never scanned, never anchored, and never reaching the `no_anchor` branch that stamps `pnl_source: unmeasured`, so it ended as a SILENT null with no provenance key. Measured 2026-09-05 over the full live journal (all 5,494 rows fetched complete by pagination; population = non-backtest, closed, intent_reduce excluded, hold computable = 1,373): 0 of 20 rows held >14d had EVER been declared, against 16 of 37 held <=14d. Verified strictly additive (9 rows gained, 0 lost) and parse-safe (0 unparseable timestamps). Guards 67/0; 312 tests pass; both controls checked by mutation rather than asserted. ⚠️ IT IS NOT MERGED AND IT IS NOT DEPLOYED. The PR is Tier-2 with landing `hold`. ⚠️ AND THE MERGE CARRIES AN OPERATOR DECISION, NOT JUST AN APPROVAL: merging IS the deploy here (ict-git-sync, ~5 min), and the approved fix is FORWARD-ONLY, so the first post-deploy tick would write 5 already-silent HISTORICAL rows (4169, 4170, 4422, 4423, 4484) — a back-fill the operator was put explicitly and did not take. Each would be filled by a sanctioned path and none can be fabricated, but the call is the operator's. ⚠️ THE SAME DEFECT CLASS SURVIVES IN TWO MORE PLACES, filed not fixed: `_sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit`'s 7-day window (costs MEASURED broker truth — worse than what MI-128 cost) and the `_LOCAL_PNL_BROKER_DEFER_MS` grace, inert for 333 of 1,204 Bybit rows (27.7%). Coordinator.multi_account_execute calls load_accounts(path) FRESH on every invocation (src/core/coordinator.py:909), and load_accounts opens and parses accounts.yaml on every call with zero cache markers (no lru_cache, no module cache, no globals — checked, not assumed); the module says so itself at :2776, 'the accounts layer is stateless per-call'. Confirmed in the ict-git-sync journal — the 21:21:48Z and 21:27:17Z ticks both logged 'Running processes already deployed ... nothing to deploy'. A successor should not read that as a stuck deploy. (3) NOT OBSERVED — STATE THE POPULATION: newest 250 `trades` rows read at 21:37Z carry ZERO rows created after the 21:33:38Z restart, and ict_scalp_5m's newest row ANYWHERE is id 5451 (bybit_portfolio, 2026-09-04T08:37:50Z). items.detail:
WHAT LANDED: src/runtime/bracket_calibration.py (pure grader, NO runtime caller), scripts/research/bracket_calibration_report.py (--exits / --mfe / --selftest), 30 tests, and docs/research/bracket-calibration-2026-09-06.md. Percent-of-entry basis, never R — the R denominator is contaminated (trades.stop_loss is the FINAL trailed stop) and the venue clamp is itself a percent of entry.

WHAT IT FOUND (populations in the memo): only 4 of 102 peak_gradeable trades (3.9%) ever reached the 9.9% level their target sits at, even at the LOWER BOUND of MFE. On the measured-exit stratum (n=82) the declared target sits at quantile 0.9024 of realised exits; on 12 donchian/pullback legs it sits at 1.0000 — not one trade in the window ended above it. Off Bybit the 0.099 cap is ~2.9x the p90 of lower-bound MFE with 0 of 39 trades ever reaching it, which ANSWERS a question src/runtime/tp_venue_cap.py declares OPEN in its own docstring.

WHY THIS ROW EXISTS AND NOT JUST A BACKLOG ROW: the specific failure that produced MI-148 was a complete specification (docs/research/EXIT-GEOMETRY-REBUILD-SESSION-PROMPT.md, 2026-08-23) that nothing pointed at, so it sat undispatched for 14 days while its diagnosis was re-established SEVEN times and built zero. A memo plus a backlog row is exactly the shape that failed. This row is the thing that puts the next step in front of a session.

THE NEXT STEP IS NAMED AND UNCLAIMED: an MFE distribution at proper n from the OFFLINE HARNESS over historical candles. The live telemetry gives 1-8 rows per leg, too thin to set a per-leg target on — doing so anyway would be the fitted-threshold failure this repo already pays for. The harness reads no live broker state and is NOT BLOCKED on anything in this thread.

DO NOT READ THIS AS 'the instrument needs proving'. It is pure, has no runtime caller, and cannot affect a live order; its --selftest asserts the recogniser fires on planted positives. What is unproven is nothing about the code — it is that the VERDICT has not reached a decision.
items.clears_when:
EITHER of two things, and say WHICH. (1) The operator makes a Tier-3 decision on the per-leg target geometry — approving a construction, rejecting it, or explicitly deciding the sentinel idiom stays — and it is RECORDED. A decision to change nothing is a legitimate outcome and clears this row; being un-actioned does not. (2) The offline-harness MFE distribution is produced at stated n and a per-leg proposal is put in front of the operator off THAT n rather than off the live 1-8.

⚠️ A RE-RUN OF THE INSTRUMENT CLEARS NOTHING. Re-measuring is precisely the failure mode this row exists to stop: the diagnosis was established seven times before it was built once. If you re-run it and the numbers hold, that is not progress — write what you saw and leave the row open.

⚠️ AND MERGING PR #11138 CLEARS NOTHING EITHER. The instrument landing is what OPENED this row, not what closes it.

items.detail:
FILED UNDER THE STANDING OPERATOR DIRECTIVE OF 2026-09-02: 'anything soaking needs to be logged with an alarm that has either a timer or a soak threshold, so that we know to get back to it when the soak is ready.'

WHY AN EMPTY SOAK IS NOT EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING YET. The consumer writes one row per evaluation to runtime_logs/ict_scalp_exit_head_soak.jsonl on EVERY outcome, including `not_scored` -- deliberately, because a soak written only when the head fires cannot tell a DEAD consumer from a SILENT one, which is exactly the distinction this path turns on today. So the file SHOULD fill immediately with not_scored rows while carrying zero firing rows. An ABSENT file means this code has never run on the VM (it needs a deploy); it never means nothing was found.

⚠️ ARMING IS TIER-3 AND IS NOT PROPOSED AS DUE. Two independent settings must both change: ICT_SCALP_EXIT_HEAD_MODE=apply AND the leg declaring exit_head_action: close in config/strategies.yaml, on top of the artifact sitting at stage advisory. Shipped state is `annotate` with NO leg declaring, so the path is byte-for-byte inert.

⚠️ AND THERE IS A STANDING OPERATOR DECISION AGAINST ARMING THESE LEGS THAT MI-146'S MEMO DOES NOT MENTION. Every one of the five candidate cells in docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json carries a 2026-08-23 `SHIP BLOCKED` operator verdict which CANCELLED the queued Tier-3 ship and named 'a consumer exists in the ict_scalp unit' as its own precondition. MI-150 satisfies that precondition and NOTHING ELSE. For ict_scalp_sol_5m the same ref records that its pass DOES NOT SURVIVE RE-PARTITIONING -- the 4-arm screen flips it to honest_negative when folds are cut 12 trades later, and its live-parity beats_hard 16/23 clears by 2 points of 46, so one fold the other way fails it (BL-20260815-SCALP-EXIT-HEAD-MATRIX-DISAGREES-WITH-THE-4-ARM-SCREEN). soak.why_a_timer_cannot_express_this: Elapsed time says nothing here, because the gating condition is not patience -- it is whether an artifact admitting a 5m/15m scalp leg has ever been published. Until one is, the tf guard refuses every leg and the log fills with not_scored rows FOREVER at any cadence. `ready` therefore has to be a FIELD VALUE (a row whose decision_state is anything other than not_scored, i.e. a leg the guard actually admitted); check_every_days says how often a session must LOOK, this says what it is looking FOR.
soak.an_empty_log_means_the_writer_is_dead_no: ⚠️ THE POLARITY IS THE OPPOSITE OF MOST SOAKS AND IS THE MOST USEFUL THING THIS BLOCK ENCODES. This consumer writes on EVERY outcome, so once it is deployed the log must fill with not_scored rows immediately. A log that is EMPTY or has stopped growing therefore means the consumer is NOT RUNNING (not deployed, or an exception path swallowing it) -- it does NOT mean the head declined to fire. Conversely a log full of not_scored rows is the HEALTHY expected state and is NOT progress toward ready.

probe.checks: A row exists in which the exit head ACTUALLY SCORED an ict_scalp leg — decision_state is one of the scored_* values, i.e. maybe_score_exit_head's in-distribution guard ADMITTED the leg and returned a record. That is the single fact this row is waiting on, and it cannot happen until a 5m/15m scalp exit-head artifact is published to the mirror.
probe.positive_control_is_the_point: ⚠️ THE EXPECTED STATE IS A LOG FULL OF `not_scored` ROWS, so a bare 'nothing matched' is indistinguishable from a fetch that returned an empty page — the `curl … || echo '{}'` defect. The positive control includes not_scored precisely so the probe must first PROVE it can read this log and find rows before its negative on the scored_* predicate means anything. Without it, a 404 (before this PR deploys the diag allowlist entry) and a genuinely unpublished artifact would grade identically.
probe.is_not: A PASS DOES NOT CLEAR THIS ROW and does not authorise arming. It establishes ONE clause: that an artifact admitting a scalp leg now exists and the consumer reached it. It says nothing about (a) whether the head is any good, (b) the 2026-08-23 SHIP BLOCKED operator decision that cancelled the Tier-3 ship, or (c) the ict_scalp_sol_5m re-partitioning failure. ⚠️ A `could_not_look` verdict (exit 2/3) is the EXPECTED result until this PR merges and deploys — the diag allowlist entry for this log ships in it — and must not be read as a negative.

items.summary: ML-2 was BUILT and REFUTED, and the refutation is the finding. Calibration PASSES on a real corpus (n=9,814 backtest trades, 3 trend_donchian 15m legs, MACE 0.0061); sharpness against the tp_r-equivalent RISK-SCALED baseline FAILS at 0 of 5 quantiles, stable across splits and identical on all three legs. So the six decision-time features carry nothing about exit location beyond volatility, tp_r is the right functional form, and what is broken is TP_VENUE_CAP_PCT destroying its scaling -- not the absence of a model. DO NOT REBUILD ML-2 on these features. Know before proposing any per-leg take-profit: the answer is a per-leg MFE quantile IN R (MI-148's proposal, unchanged), and gate condition 1 (backtest-live exit-location fidelity) is a SEPARATE and still-unmet condition.

A row reading `unanchored` or `no_risk` is turtle_soup/vwap behaving correctly and says nothing about these nine. The positive control (`peak_state` present with ANY of its four values) separates 'the nine have not emitted yet' from 'the endpoint is unreadable or empty' -- it should match today on trend_donchian / htf_pullback_trend_2h rows, which have carried the hook all along, so a control that does NOT match means the probe is blind, not that the nine are silent.
probe.is_not: A PASS DOES NOT CLEAR THIS ROW, and establishes less than it looks like. (1) It is ONE row, not a corpus: MI-163's own gradeability floor is n=30 pooled, so a single measured peak makes the nine VISIBLE without making the ict_scalp one-shot mechanism MEASURED -- which was the point of hooking them. (2) peak_r is a LOWER BOUND by construction (peak_provenance: estimated); a bar-extreme peak cannot see an intrabar excursion. (3) It reads the telemetry table, never the venue, so it cannot say the peak matches what the position actually did. (4) It says nothing about Proposal B, which stays unbuilt and un-numbered.

items.title: The netting reconciler is closing LIVE Bybit positions because it grades a symbol off get_positions rows[0] and a hedge book reads flat — three provable false closes, one open right now, and real money is in the exposed population
items.summary: TWO FACTS, and neither is the orphan the operator was alerted about. (1) ROOT CAUSE, UNFIXED AND LIVE: src/runtime/order_monitor.py:8821 does `pos = rows[0]` on a symbol-scoped get_positions with no zero-size skip and no hedge-book selection. Since BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS was armed 2026-08-30 a symbol carries two books and Bybit returns a row for each including the empty one, so a zero-size sibling listed first makes _bybit_position_protection return _flat for a symbol that is NOT flat. _reconcile_netting_partial_closes then reads backed=0.0, excess=the whole journal row, and closes a live position with an ESTIMATED pnl. MEASURED end to end on trade 5568 (bybit_1 ETHUSDT long 26.05): the soak row at 14:24:09Z carries exchange_qty 0.0 / attributed_qty 26.05 / basis leg_gone, while the venue held Buy 26.05 @ 2476.6 continuously across four reads 14:31:27Z-14:43:35Z and 5568's own tracked SL leg 7b5af72f was still resting Untriggered. It booked a fabricated +$63.8225. (2) CONTAINMENT IS ALSO ABSENT: _recently_closed_adopted_orphan's exit_reason allowlist omits 'netting_attributed', so the BL-20260618-RECONCILE-DUP flap guard cannot see this class at all and the position is re-adopted as a fresh row 3-4 minutes later. That is verbatim the gap the function's own docstring records being closed for two OTHER reasons by BL-20260707. SO THE ORPHAN ALERT WAS A SYMPTOM. Trade 5569 is correctly reconcile_status 'reconciled' against a correctly-named package (pkg-5c339e25d5144c32, verified three ways) — the row should never have existed. Do NOT re-stamp it; that hides the incident. REAL MONEY IS IN THE EXPOSED POPULATION AND WAS NOT EXPOSED-AND-SAFE: 7 of 49 netting_attributed closes in the measured window are on bybit_2, and trade 5461 (2026-09-04T12:34:25Z, XRPUSDT long 69.4) is an exchange_qty 0.0 flat read on an account where XRP is hedge-armed. I did NOT establish whether that particular close was wrong — no adopt followed it — which is a gap in the evidence, not a clean bill. THREE PROVABLE FALSE CLOSES total (+$115.8575 of manufactured ESTIMATED pnl): 5515->5516, 5554->5555, 5568->5569, each an exact-size adopt within 4 minutes. THREE IS A LOWER BOUND: 12 of 21 applied soak rows read exchange_qty 0.0 and the soak carries no position_idx and no source, so the other nine are UNGRADEABLE from any repo surface. Nothing is armed, cancelled or repaired; all fixes are proposals.
items.clears_when: THREE PARTS, and they are different facts — say WHICH you cleared rather than clearing the row on the easiest. (1) THE ROOT CAUSE LANDS: _bybit_position_protection selects the book instead of taking rows[0], AND its two collapses are separated — `not rows` on a symbol-scoped call returns None (we could not look) rather than _flat, and more than one LIVE book returns None rather than picking one. (2) THE FIX IS OBSERVED ON THE FLEET, which is a DIFFERENT fact from (1): a netting_attribution_soak row on a hedge-armed symbol carrying a non-zero exchange_qty where the venue holds a position, AND no further netting_attributed -> same-size-adopt pair. [!] A PASSING UNIT TEST CLEARS NEITHER — a fixture cannot reproduce which row Bybit lists first, which is the whole mechanism. [!] AND THE ABSENCE OF NEW ADOPT PAIRS IS NOT SUFFICIENT ALONE: the flap needs a second live position in the sibling book to arise at all, so a quiet week may mean the condition did not occur rather than that it is fixed. Say which you established. (3) THE NINE UNGRADEABLE FLAT READS ARE GRADED, or the soak is given `source` + `position_idx` so they become gradeable and the count is recorded. That count is what a NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_MODE widening decision actually rests on and nobody has it. [!] THE OPEN ETHUSDT POSITION CLOSING DOES NOT CLEAR ANY PART OF THIS. It will close eventually by TP, SL or a strategy exit, and that says nothing about the reconciler. If it closes with an UNEXPLAINED resolution, record THAT rather than clearing on it — an unexplained resolution is not evidence the mechanism works (the PROTECTION_REASSERT_MODE lesson in CLAUDE.md, whose one live exhibit vanished with the cause unestablished). [!] AND RE-STAMPING TRADE 5569 CLEARS NOTHING. It is already correctly `reconciled`.

The observable is which row Bybit's live API lists first for a hedge-armed symbol; CI holds no exchange credentials, does not run the monitor tick, and a fixture cannot reproduce venue row ordering — a harness can only re-assert assertions that already pass, which is the 'green while measuring nothing' failure. NO PROBE EXISTS AND THE HALF THAT MATTERS CANNOT HAVE ONE, which is a property of the condition rather than of the effort available. Clause (a) asks whether a GitHub Actions run of e35-bracket-sweep.yml SCHEDULED both legs and its fetch step returned real rows — that lives in a run log and in `actions_list`, and CI holds no mcp__github__* tool, so a probe running IN CI cannot read it. ⚠️ AND THE OBVIOUS SUBSTITUTE IS THE TRAP THIS ROW IS ABOUT: a probe that re-ran the planner and asserted `resolve_feed_source('QLD','D') == 'yfinance'` would go GREEN on the code being merged while the runner path stayed unexercised — the planner selftest already asserts exactly that, 66 cases pass, and a harness is precisely what cannot reach a runner or Yahoo's rate limiter. A green probe would therefore report the thing this row exists to say is UNPROVEN. Clause (b) is an operator decision on a Tier-3 config change and is not probeable by construction.
