items.summary: TWO MEASUREMENT TRAPS ON THE REAL-MONEY TRADE SURFACE, both of which have ALREADY produced a wrong operator-facing conclusion (2026-09-08, MI-200). Read this BEFORE measuring real-money performance. (1) THE POPULATION. GET /api/bot/trades/closed takes include_paper, DEFAULT False, so the default response is ALREADY real-money-only. Passing include_paper=true and then filtering to accountClass=='real_money' does NOT widen the real-money set — it NARROWS it to whatever fraction of the newest `limit` MIXED rows happens to be real money. Measured: ?limit=200 -> 200 real-money rows; ?limit=200&include_paper=true -> 15 real-money rows; paged to exhaustion -> 447, window 2026-05-09..2026-09-04. A dispatch reported the 15 as 'the real-money population' and concluded '0 wins, 13 losses'. The book is actually 117 W / 258 L / 49 flat (n=424 graded). The failure is SILENT: 200 OK, every row genuinely real money, nothing says the set was truncated. (2) THE LABEL. `closeReason` on that route folds FIFTEEN distinct mechanisms into `other`, including 182 rows that ARE strategy exits (vwap_cross, sl_cross, tp_cross, exit_head, time_decay, stale_stop). Reading `other` as 'not a strategy exit' is wrong in BOTH directions. /api/bot/strategies uses a DIFFERENT taxonomy over the SAME column and the two disagree on 174 of 447 rows (38.9%); 53 rows read `sl` on one surface and `other` on the other. Read RAW trades.exit_reason, never closeReason, to answer 'did the strategy's exit fire?'.

If either premise is wrong, the change trades a noisy alarm for a silent one, and the silent one is worse.

soak.why_a_timer_cannot_express_this: The question is not how long the reader has run but WHICH of three states it saw, and the deciding state is rare by construction -- it needs two simultaneously non-zero books on one symbol, which requires hedge mode armed on that symbol AND both books live at the same instant. Elapsed days cannot distinguish 'the condition has not occurred' from 'the writer is dead', and those demand opposite responses: the first RETIRES a Tier-3 proposal, the second is a deploy defect. check_every_days says how often a session must LOOK; this says what it looks FOR. The negative outcome is deliberately given a clearing path of its own, because a soak whose only exit is 'the bad thing happened' runs forever when the bad thing never does -- which is how a held decision becomes an abandoned one.

Write it into observation, keep the row open, and say so loudly -- the leg is then still oversized, which is today's behaviour, so nothing regressed but nothing was fixed either. !! A GREEN TEST SUITE CLEARS NOTHING (20 tests and a 39/39 self-test already pass, and neither can reach a venue). !! AND `not_applicable` ON EVERY REDUCE IS ITS OWN FINDING, not a pass: it would mean BYBIT_TPSL_MODE is no longer `partial`, in which case the per-row leg does not exist and this row should be RECORDED as retired-by-configuration rather than left looking like a fix awaiting evidence.

items.probe_absent_reason: NO PROBE EXISTS AND ONE CANNOT BE WRITTEN THAT WOULD CLEAR THIS ROW, and that is a property of the condition rather than of the effort available. Both clearing outcomes are acts nothing in this repo may perform. (a) EXERCISED requires `MULTI_STRATEGY_INTENT_LAYER=false` to be SET on a trader -- a Tier-2 VM mutation, not covered by this build's approval -- and then a tick OBSERVED under it. A probe cannot set the flag, and must not: a probe that armed a rollback on a live trader to satisfy its own row would be the worst instrument in this repo. (b) RETIRED is an operator DECISION, which no probe can read. !! AND A PROBE OF THE ONE THING THAT IS MECHANICALLY CHECKABLE WOULD BE ACTIVELY MISLEADING: `pipeline.strategy_builders()` covering all 45 execution:live legs is already asserted every CI run by tests/test_strategy_builder_registry_single_home.py::test_every_live_leg_is_buildable_on_both_paths, so such a probe would report a durable green about REGISTRATION while this row is open on EXERCISE. That is the shape the probe contract's own `is_not` field exists to prevent, and here it is cheaper to declare no probe than to ship one whose pass means something other than what the row asks. The row is bounded by check_every_days instead: a session must LOOK every 7 days and say which of (a) or (b) it established, or that it established neither.

NO PROBE TODAY, AND THE REASON IS A BUILDABLE GAP IN OUR OWN READER -- NOT A PROPERTY OF THE CONDITION, and it is written that way deliberately. probe_api.py's own docstring records that two earlier probe_absent_reason texts blamed a missing BEARER when the real blocker was a missing FETCHER, i.e. 'a buildable gap wearing the label of a permanent one, which is why those two reasons had to be corrected rather than merely re-worded'. This one names its gap so nobody has to correct it later. THE GAP: the grade this row waits on is summary.restart_gap.restart_gap_state on /api/bot/exit-interval/soak, and probe_api.fetch_rows resolves a dict payload by taking the first of records/rows/lines/reports/banners/results that is a list -- so on this route it reads `records`, the RAW per-interval rows, and the summary is never addressed. The raw rows carry process_started_utc and first_pass_of_process but NOT the grade. !! SO THE PROBE THAT IS EASY TO WRITE IS THE WRONG ONE: requiring first_pass_of_process=true would pass as soon as any process boundary appears in the log, which proves a boundary EXISTS and says nothing about whether the gap across it was graded -- a probe whose pass means something other than what the row asks, which this register already judges worse than no probe. THE FIX, for whoever wants it: teach probe_api to address a nested object (a --object-path or equivalent), then probe restart_gap_state~within,near_miss,breached with a positive control of restart_gap_state~within,near_miss,breached,not_measured,unknown. That is a real, small piece of work and is NOT being done here only because the field is not deployed yet, so the probe could not be verified against a live payload and would ship as an unproven arm. !! AND EVEN WITH THAT READER, THE PROBE COULD ONLY CLEAR CLAUSE (2): clause (3) needs a max_interval_ms in [54s, 60s], which is rare BY DESIGN (once in the n=989 window), so a silent probe there would be the fix working rather than evidence -- the shape OI-20260906-BYBIT-CLOSE-QTY-SNAP already records. The row is bounded by check_every_days instead: a session must LOOK every 7 days and say which clause it established, or that it established none.

Absence proves nothing here: these are four 1d legs whose pooled historical rate is ~6 long packages per 101 days, and the SHORT side is unexecutable at the venue (shorting_enabled: false), so a quiet window cannot distinguish 'the wiring failed' from 'no long setup occurred'. Establish the positive control FIRST -- that at least one of the four produced a LONG package on alpaca_paper or alpaca_portfolio across the same window -- and report BOTH numbers. Without that control, record the outcome as `not_yet_observed`, which is a THIRD state and is neither a pass nor a failure. ⚠️ A GREEN TEST SUITE CLEARS NOTHING: the mirror invariant and the roster tests pass in a harness and a harness cannot reach a venue. ⚠️ AND silent_refusal_alert GRADING THIS ACCOUNT HEALTHY CLEARS NOTHING EITHER until #11666 has merged AND the trader has restarted onto it -- until then its latch for alpaca_live is immortal and says nothing about today. ⚠️ IF A LONG DOES DISPATCH AND IS REFUSED, OR FILLS AND FAILS TO RECONCILE, that does NOT clear this row and is the MORE VALUABLE finding -- it is the first exercise of an order path that has never been exercised on this account. Write it into `observation` and keep the row open. ⚠️ IF THE OPERATOR REVERSES and removes any of the four, this row does NOT clear -- it CHANGES: that is a legitimate Tier-3 decision and must be RECORDED as one rather than left looking like a wiring change about to take effect.
items.probe_absent_reason: PARTIAL CAPABILITY, stated rather than hidden. Clause (2) IS probeable from a session (/api/diag/version), and clause (1) is a GitHub state no repo-side probe reaches. Clause (3) is deliberately NOT given a probe: the honest form is a JOIN of two populations -- zero alpaca_live rows for the four legs, measured against a window in which at least one of them demonstrably produced a LONG package on a paper book -- and a probe asserting only 'no alpaca_live rows yet' would go green through every quiet spell, which is the vacuous-negative class CLAUDE.md section 'Green is not evidence' names. At a pooled rate of ~6 long packages per 101 days that quiet spell is the NORMAL state for weeks, so such a probe would be wrong almost all of the time while looking healthy. Left to a session that can state both denominators.

items.title: The orphan-adopt size gate is MERGED and DEPLOYED, and has refused nothing -- three different facts, and only the third is still open
items.summary: MI-255 (Tier-2, operator-approved via the manager 2026-09-10, PR #11708) added a size-plausibility gate to the orphan-adopt attribution path: src/runtime/orphan_attribution.py (a pure decision, four never-collapsed states) consulted at the two sites that WRITE trades.strategy_name. It fixes BL-20260908-THE-ORPHAN-ADOPT-REATTACH-WRITES-A-STRATEGY-NAME-IT-CANNOT-SUPPORT-AND-THAT-STRATEGY-THEN-ACTS-ON-THE-ROW, whose defect is that _recover_orphan_order_package matched on (symbol, direction, entry_price) with NO size term, and the strategy it named then ran its own monitor() against the position. !! MERGED IS NOT DEPLOYED AND DEPLOYED IS NOT OBSERVED -- three facts, and the first two are now settled. Merged as 55f082e66. !! CORRECTED 2026-09-10T17:06:06Z, AND THIS ROW'S ID WAS RENAMED WITH IT (it read ...-MERGED-NOT-DEPLOYED-... and had never landed on main, so no reference could break; the original text is preserved here rather than deleted). THE DEPLOY HALF IS NOW OBSERVED POSITIVE: /api/diag/version reads git_sha 55f082e66 -- the merge commit itself -- with git_sha_on_disk b8cbbbf10, which also contains it by ancestry. THE ORIGINAL READING WAS TAKEN AT 2026-09-10T16:49:53Z AND WAS CORRECT WHEN TAKEN: git_sha 25a60f068 / git_sha_on_disk efc5e2958, NEITHER containing 55f082e66 -- i.e. ict-git-sync closed the gap in the ~16 minutes between the two reads, which is the ~5-minute pull cadence behaving as documented. It is recorded because 'the PR merged' is what a session would otherwise carry forward as if it meant the code was live, and because the negative-then-positive pair is the evidence that the deploy was WATCHED rather than assumed. !! AND THE GATE HAS NEVER REFUSED ANYTHING. It is a REFUSAL TEST that fires only when a candidate package exists AND the claimed strategy's own size history on that symbol excludes the position, so it is RARE BY CONSTRUCTION. !! CORRECTED 2026-09-10, AND THE CORRECTION MAKES THE GATE RARER, NOT COMMONER: this read '2 of 5 judgeable adopts over the measured window', a figure with NO STATED POPULATION -- the one rule this repo promoted to top level. Re-measured by grading EVERY named adopt with the deployed module over a population that IS stated (the 1000 rows /api/diag/journal returns for trades, ids 4653..5652): 15 carry setup_type='adopted_orphan', all 15 name a strategy, ZERO are bare, and the verdicts are 13 supported / 2 size_implausible (5448, 5453) / 0 no_history / 0 unreadable. So it is 2 of 15, ~3x rarer than the original figure implies. !! THAT DIRECTION IS THE POINT: the rarer the refusal, the WEAKER 'no refusals seen' is as evidence the gate works, which is this row's whole thesis. !! AND THE ORIGINAL FIGURE IS NOT THEREBY WRONG -- its population was never recorded, so the two cannot be compared; that absence IS the defect. !! 2-of-15 is an UPPER BOUND on refusals: history enters only via min and max, so more history can only WIDEN the band, leaving a supported verdict stable and softening an implausible one. The runtime gate reads a THIRD basis again (limit=200 per strategy+symbol). Name the population whenever this number is quoted.
items.observation: 2026-09-10 by session_01FyYyybxWC7VD1Rq1doEEdf. !! I CLEARED THE DEPLOY HALF AND NOTHING ELSE -- naming WHICH half is what this row's own clears_when demands. OBSERVED: /api/diag/version at 17:06:06Z reads git_sha 55f082e66, the merge commit itself, so the RUNNING trader carries the gate; a read 16 minutes earlier read 25a60f068 and did not, so the deploy was WATCHED rather than assumed. A deploy is the WEAKER of the two facts this row tracks: it says the code CAN run, never that it ran. THE REFUSAL HAS BEEN OBSERVED BY NOBODY, so the row stays open on its real criterion. Otherwise established, and only what a repo surface can establish -- the merge (55f082e66, verified on origin/main directly, all three call sites wired at order_monitor.py:3229, :3955, :4210), full CI green including a ~20-minute pytest-run over the whole suite, guards PASS 70 / FAIL 0. !! verified_at STAYS null, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE REFUSAL A LATER SESSION SHOULD NOT 'HELPFULLY' UNDO -- I set it to today, re-read this row's own criterion, and put it back. Dating it suppresses the row from the DUE list for its full 3-day cadence on the strength of a DEPLOY READ, which is not an observation of this row's SUBJECT. The subject is a refusal on the fleet and nobody has looked for one. A row whose criterion has never been looked for should render in EVERY session brief, not every third one; `never` is the truthful value and it is what keeps the row in front of somebody. !! ONE THING WORTH CARRYING: THE OBVIOUS IMPLEMENTATION OF THIS GATE FLATTENS LIVE POSITIONS, and it was built that way first before being caught by reading the function. _reattach_adopted_orphans' own docstring says an UN-RECOVERABLE orphan is FLATTENED by the caller's per-account pass, so a refusal reported as a plain None is indistinguishable from 'no candidate exists' and becomes a live reduce-only close. That is why the helper returns a typed _OrphanAttribution and why the flatten probe consults the gate NOT to refuse anything. A future change that 'simplifies' the return type back to Optional[dict] RE-ARMS THAT HAZARD.
items.clears_when: A LIVE ADOPT IS OBSERVED DECLINING -- a trades row with setup_type='adopted_orphan' and strategy_name='orphan_adopt' (the bare state) for a position where a price-matching candidate package DID exist, read from the live journal. That is the backlog row's own bar and it says so in terms: 'not by a unit test, which cannot reproduce the venue state that produces a candidate package'. !! A GREEN TEST SUITE CLEARS NOTHING: 24 tests pass and both load-bearing properties are mutation-checked, and a harness cannot reach a venue -- which is precisely why this row exists beside the green PR. !! MERGING CLEARS NOTHING -- that is what this row already records. !! THE DEPLOY IS A SEPARATE, WEAKER FACT AND IT IS ALREADY CLEARED -- do not spend a cycle re-reading it: /api/diag/version read git_sha 55f082e66 at 2026-09-10T17:06:06Z (see observation), which clears the DEPLOY half ONLY. Say WHICH half you cleared. What is outstanding is the paragraph above this one, and only that. !! A QUIET PERIOD IS NOT EVIDENCE EITHER: the refusal is rare by construction, so 'no refusals seen' cannot distinguish a working gate from an inert one -- establish that adopts are still HAPPENING at all before reading zero refusals as anything. !! IF A REFUSAL IS OBSERVED AND THE POSITION IS THEN FLATTENED, that does NOT clear this row and is the far more valuable finding -- the refused/no-candidate distinction failed somewhere -- so write it into observation and keep the row open.
items.why_it_matters: A Tier-2 change to the reconciler that decides adoptions and closes on LIVE positions, on a code path that reads NO account field -- so bybit_2 (real money) is on it exactly as bybit_1 (demo) is. The measured harm to date is demo-only and is CONTAMINATION rather than loss (trade 5453: +612.705681 of phantom PROFIT booked onto pairs_sol_eth_b, is_demo=1), but the mechanism is account-blind. A gate that is merged, believed live, and in fact neither deployed nor exercised is the exact looks-armed-is-not state this register exists to keep visible.
items.probe_absent_reason: NO PROBE IS POSSIBLE YET AND THE REASON IS DATED, NOT PERMANENT. The gate emits a logger.warning on refusal and writes no soak file, so there is no allowlisted diag surface to read: a probe written today would grade could_not_read forever while LOOKING like a quiet negative. A soak was deliberately NOT added because the refusal is expected to be rare, and a soak that is empty by design cannot be told apart from a writer that is not writing. The honest instrument is the journal itself: a bare orphan whose candidate existed.

items.title: R2, the per-pass IB circuit breaker, is armed by default and has never skipped a package -- and the 60s promise is NOT thereby fixed
items.summary: MI-240 (Tier-2, operator-approved as DEC-20260910-EXIT-EVAL-60S-REMEDY, chosen `r2_only`, 2026-09-10T07:52Z) arms R2: once ONE IB-routed fetch in an exit-evaluation pass returns a pinned-thread QUEUE timeout, the remaining IB-routed fetches in THAT pass are skipped and their callers get candles=None. It bounds the COST of an outcome already determined -- IB market data is serialised on one pinned worker (_IB_FETCH_EXECUTOR, max_workers=1), so while that queue is congested every later fetch waits its own 29.0s and returns None anyway. !! THE EVIDENCE IS A COMPLETE CENSUS, NOT A SAMPLE, AND IT IS WORTH RE-READING BEFORE ACTING ON THIS ROW: docs/claude/work/EXIT-EVAL-60S-ROOTCAUSE-2026-09-10.md, all 1218 within-process breaching intervals read 2026-09-10T06:13Z from /api/bot/exit-interval/soak. Every within-process 60s breach is a slow PASS (1218/1218 pass_ms > 30s; ZERO rows carry a residual above one cadence period, so no scheduler-stall hypothesis survives), and the live residual is 10 of 14 post-fix breaches inside the 04:00-05:00Z IBKR reset window -- 71.4% against 8.6% for the flat pre-fix population -- where a pass costs n_IB x 29s and crosses 60s at THREE packages. INFERRED from that arithmetic: window pass cost falls from n x 29s to ~35s. !! ARMED IS NOT EXERCISED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT THIS ROW WATCHES. No live pass has been observed being skipped by it. The trip is RARE BY CONSTRUCTION -- it needs a genuinely congested pinned queue, which the census puts almost entirely inside one hour a day -- so the rarer it is, the WEAKER 'no skips seen' is as evidence that it works. !! AND THE 60s PROMISE IS NOT FIXED. R2 targets the WITHIN-PROCESS residual only. R1 (moving _start_exit_loop above _apply_per_account_leverage) was OFFERED and NOT chosen and is not in the diff; whether the RESTART BOUNDARY is in scope for the 60s requirement at all was option 4 and was ALSO not chosen, so it is unsettled rather than settled by implication. The restart-boundary population is untouched by this change -- 444 of 444 measured boundaries, 77 breaching (17.3%), max 210,409.2 ms. Anyone reading this row as 'the exit-eval breaches are dealt with' is reading it wrong.
items.observation: 2026-09-10, session_01CTPC91xaHrK6ES33UKjkTY, AT THE MOMENT OF FILING -- so this is a BASELINE, not a check of the mechanism, and the row's cadence starts from here. WHAT WAS SEEN: nothing on the fleet. The change is not merged, therefore not deployed, therefore no pass has run under it, and no ib_breaker field can exist on any exit_interval_soak row yet. Stated positively rather than left blank so a later session cannot mistake the absence for a measurement: at filing time, clauses (1), (2) and (3) of clears_when are ALL unmet, and the correct reading of a zero here is 'the code is not there', never 'the breaker saw a healthy queue'. WHAT *WAS* ESTABLISHED, in a harness and only in a harness: 27 assertions pass, and the two load-bearing properties are mutation-checked -- making the breaker trip on a bare None fails 1 test, hoisting its state out of the per-pass closure fails 4. That says the DECISION is pinned. It says nothing whatever about a wedged IB queue, which no harness can reach.
items.clears_when: A PASS IS OBSERVED BEING SHORTENED BY THE BREAKER, end to end on the fleet, and it is THREE facts -- say WHICH you cleared rather than clearing the row on the easiest. (1) DEPLOYED: /api/diag/version reports a git_sha that CONTAINS the merge commit (check ANCESTRY, not string equality -- main moves fast and the trader pulls every ~5 min). (2) ARMED: EXIT_LOOP_IB_BREAKER_DISABLED read off /proc/<MainPID>/environ via get-env and found ABSENT (or explicitly falsy). !! NEVER OFF THE .env, which says only what the NEXT restart picks up. !! AN UNSET VALUE IS THE ARMED STATE, so 'the key is not there' is the PASS here, not a failed read -- which is exactly why the key was added to get_env.py::ALLOWED_KEYS in the same change. (3) EXERCISED: an exit-interval soak row is observed carrying ib_breaker.state='armed' with tripped=true and skipped>0 -- read off /api/bot/exit-interval/soak or /api/diag/log_file?name=exit_interval_soak. Record that row's pass_ms beside the n it skipped: the predicted shape is ~35s rather than n x 29s. !! A GREEN TEST SUITE CLEARS NOTHING. 27 assertions pass and both load-bearing properties are mutation-checked, and a harness cannot reach a wedged IB queue -- which IS the condition. !! MERGING CLEARS NOTHING: a merge is not a deploy and a deploy is not an observed pass. !! A QUIET WINDOW IS NOT EVIDENCE EITHER, and it is the likeliest reading to get wrong. The trip is rare by construction, so 'no skips seen' cannot distinguish a working breaker from an inert one. ESTABLISH THE DENOMINATOR FIRST: confirm rows exist carrying ib_breaker.state='armed' with skipped=0 -- that is the breaker LIVE and the queue HEALTHY, and without it a run of zeros is indistinguishable from the field never being written. state='no_ib_packages' is a THIRD thing (nothing IB-routed in that pass) and must not be pooled with either. !! ZERO ROWS CARRYING ANY ib_breaker FIELD AFTER A FULL PASS CADENCE IS A DEPLOY DEFECT, the OPPOSITE fact from a quiet queue, and must never be reported as 'no skips observed'. !! AND IF A SKIP IS OBSERVED AND AN EXIT IS THEN MISSED ON THAT SYMBOL, that does NOT clear this row and is the far more valuable finding -- the transient-vs-congested distinction failed -- so write it into observation and keep the row open. !! IF THE OPERATOR ROLLS IT BACK (EXIT_LOOP_IB_BREAKER_DISABLED truthy), this row does NOT clear -- it CHANGES: the reset-window pass cost is then accepted as n x 29s, which is a legitimate Tier-2 decision and must be RECORDED as one rather than left looking like a breaker about to prove itself.
items.why_it_matters: It is a change to the live EXIT-EVALUATION path -- the thing that decides when an open position is re-examined -- and the code path reads no account field, so real-money bybit_2 positions ride it exactly as demo ones do. The change is deliberately outcome-neutral (a skipped package gets the same candles=None it would have got 29s later), but 'deliberately' is a claim about the design and not an observation of the fleet. The stated, accepted cost is real: during a TRANSIENT single-fetch queue timeout that is not congestion, the breaker skips later IB packages that might have succeeded; they get candles=None for one pass and are retried ~30s later. That is why it is Tier-2 and why it is watched rather than assumed.
items.probe_absent_reason: NO PROBE IS DECLARED, AND THE REASON IS THAT EVERY AVAILABLE PREDICATE WOULD LIE IN THE REASSURING DIRECTION. The breaker writes no soak file of its own -- deliberately: a trip is rare by construction, so a dedicated log would be EMPTY for long stretches and 'empty by design' cannot be told from 'the writer is dead', which is the exact collapse a soak alarm exists to prevent. The verdict is instead stamped onto the EXISTING per-pass exit_interval_soak row, which writes every pass regardless -- so a not_writing verdict against that log would grade the exit loop's liveness, never the breaker's, and would read healthy forever. What a session must do here is a READ with a stated denominator (clause 3 above), not a predicate. A probe becomes possible once a trip has been seen at least once and its row shape is confirmed against live data rather than against a test fixture.

there_is_no_cap: Deliberately UNCAPPED (operator-directed 2026-08-26: 'we don't want to cap the number of bugs we can track, we want to ensure that they are actually being tracked, fixed, and learned from'). An earlier version capped this at 12 rows; that was a bandaid — it bounded the LIST rather than making anything get read or fixed. What bounds it instead is that a `monitoring` row must be RE-OBSERVED on a cadence: it cannot be carried by doing nothing.
monitoring_rows_are_enforced_by_observat: kind:'monitoring' rows carry `check_every_days`, `verified_at` and `observation`. A row past its cadence is DUE and is rendered into CLAUDE.md, so the next session sees it in context before acting. Clearing it for another cycle costs one honest look: record WHAT YOU OBSERVED and today's date. It cannot be cleared by asserting progress — `observation` must state a thing that was seen. This replaces `loud`, which was just another alarm to walk past.
probes_report_they_never_clear: A `monitoring` row may carry `probe` (a declared command that OBSERVES something, run by scripts/ops/run_probes.py) or `probe_absent_reason` (why none exists), never both and never neither — so 'nothing probes this' stays distinguishable from 'a probe ran and was quiet'. A probe REPORTS; only a SESSION clears a row. Every probe therefore declares `is_not`: what a PASS still does not establish. The hazard is not a broken probe, it is a working one read as proof the row cleared.
